projects.summary: 这是什么 一套完全从零自研的本地 AI 全栈：推理引擎、插件总线、爬虫、知识库、Web UI、训练管线，全部手写，AGPL-3.0 开源。没有 llama.cpp、没有 PyTorch（训练对账用完即弃，产物零外部运行时）、没有任何第三方依赖——每一层都是可审计的纯 C / 纯 stdlib 代码。 我们做了什么 纯 C 推理引擎：三值量化核（1.58-bit）+ SIMD 快路径，权重自定义 2-bit 打包格式（.aimw） 权重转换器：微软 BitNet 官方 gguf → .aimw，一条命令完成 插件总线：约 100 行 C 实现，caps.json 注册表 → 拉起 Python 插件 → JSON 信封通信；模型不感知插件，确定性路由决定调用 多引擎爬虫：bing/百度/360 并行 + Edge 渲染级联（JS 重站点自动升级渲染），robots.txt 遵守 + 质量五信号闸（残文长度/壳密度/句子结构/信息密度/菜单味），fail-closed 知识库：FTS5 全文索引 + 查重闸，中文维基 dump 自建（CC-BY-SA 署名） 本地 Web UI：纯 stdlib，127.0.0.1:8600，对话直答 / 知识库引答 / 联网搜索→爬取→入库→引答全链路 训练管线：无自动微分训练栈（手写反向传播，29 参数 selftest 对账相对误差 5.7e-7）、十科课程生成器、语料构建器 117 章研究日志：SIMD 逐位对账、投机解码熔核、负面结果档案全部公开 实测结果 | 项目 | 数字 | |---|---| | 三值核 SIMD 快路径 | 85.53 tok/s（从 2.08 优化 41 倍） | | BitNet b1.58-2B-4T 推理 | 3.20 tok/s（双工人；串行 1.99） | | 权重体积 | 0.87 GB（.aimw 格式） | | C/NumPy 逐位对账 | 全绿（差一个 bit 不许提交） | | HF 贪心解码对账 | 前 9 token 逐位一致 | 测试配置（就是一台 2018 年的老笔记本） | 部件 | 规格 | |---|---| | CPU | Intel Core i7-7500U @ 2.70GHz（2 核 4 线程，低压 U） | | 内存 | 8GB DDR4-2133 单通道 | | GPU | GeForce 940MX（太弱，弃用——整套栈纯 CPU） | | 系统 | Windows | 优势 1. 断供免疫：全栈自研零第三方依赖，断网可运行、自主可服务，关键路径全部 vendor 进自家仓库 2. 全层可审计：引擎到 UI 每一层一个下午能读完，bug 可定位 3. 硬件门槛极低：2018 年双核低压 U 就能跑 2B 模型，多核/AVX-512/大内存机器欢迎帮忙测上限（我们没条件验证） 4. 训练资产全公开：课程生成器、语料构建器、正负面结果一起发——负面结果档案可能是仓库里最值钱的部分 5. 诚实文化：自研分词器未完成全量验证就明说，第三方权重配套微软官方分词器 诚实边界 2B 是这套硬件的舒适上限 自研 152M 模型还在训练（免费云容器），权重未发布，管线与证据全公开 Windows 优先（渲染级联用 Edge），Linux 编译通过、级联需装 Chromium 7 分钟演示视频在 README 顶部（实机录屏：对话 / 知识库引答 / 联网全链）。AGPL-3.0，研究文档 CC-BY-NC，微软权重 MIT 归属声明见 NOTICE.md。

projects.author: _fat_santa
projects.summary: Hey everyone, I've been very interested in software factories lately but every time I've read about them, I see folks talking alot about high level concepts and the idea of a software factory but never actually walk you through how to set one up. Or if they do walk you through how to set one up, it's always overly complicated and requires a ton of up-front investment to get things running. In response to this I built rowbly, a CLI that tries to make it as easy as possible to understand and setup a software factory. Rowbly at it's core works like a kanban board and each column can contain an optional prompt that instructs an agent what to do when a story is within this column. Once you have some stories on your board you run a supervisor skill that monitors the board for changes and spawns agents to work on stories within each column. The default configuration ships with 5 columns: backlog, refinement, development, review and done. Once a story is moved into refinement, the supervisor automatically dispatches an agent to refine the story based on the instructions in that column. When refinement is finished the ticket is automatically pushed into the development column when another agent is spawned, then into review and finally into done when the PR is merged. While this is a default configuration, things can get much more exotic based on how things are setup. Each column prompt will define where the story goes after it's finished in that column, so you could wire up a very sophisticated setup, review loops, security scans, testing, etc. From a data perspective I tried to keep things as simple as possible, all data is stored in plain markdown and json files in the folder where you initialize rowbly. If you're interested you can run it directly with npx using: `npx rowbly` or install globally with `npm install -g rowbly`. When you run it for the first time, it will walk you through adding stages, prompts and companion skills but all of this can be modified to your liking. Github Repo: https://github.com/sgolovine/rowbly/

projects.title: Casvisor： JumpServer 之外的开源堡垒机， Apache-2.0，一个 Go 二进制装下 SSH / RDP / VNC / Telnet
projects.author: Casbin
projects.summary: 团队里管着几十台服务器，最后都会走到同一个问题：谁在什么时候连了哪台机器，做了什么？ 常见的做法是共享账号、把 SSH 密码发在群里，或者大家一起用同一个跳板机账号。真出了事，登录日志里只有一行 IP ，查不到人；有人把密码带走，也无从知道。 堡垒机就是解决这个的。但看了一圈开源的选项： - JumpServer：国内事实标准，但 RDP 代理、数据库的原生客户端代理（ Magnus ）、远程应用这些放在企业版里； - Teleport：AGPL ，社区版二进制对企业规模和收入有限制； - Next Terminal：2.0 起服务端闭源，免费版限 100 个资产； - Boundary：仓库已经归档； - Warpgate：Apache-2.0 ，Rust ，单二进制，是目前最接近「完全开源」的对手。 我们想要的是：功能完整、一个二进制就能跑、能接自己的 SSO 。找不到，就自己写了 Casvisor 。 ### 连接 **SSH**：网页里是 xterm.js 终端，旁边带一个文件面板，走 SFTP 上传下载。 **RDP**：自己写的纯 Go 客户端 [gordp]( https://github.com/casvisor/gordp)，支持 NLA 、GFX 图形管道（ ClearCodec 和 RemoteFX Progressive ，和 Windows 自带客户端一样的画质路径）、高 DPI 下的清晰字体、远程光标、剪贴板、跟随窗口改大小、通过重定向的磁盘传文件。Windows Server 、Windows 10/11 都连过，FreeRDP 那一类主机也能连。 **VNC**：noVNC ，VNC 的认证由后端做，浏览器拿不到 VNC 密码。 **Telnet**：给交换机、老设备用，自动填资产里存的账号。 **SSH 网关**：`ssh -p 2222 web-01@casvisor.example.com`，scp 、sftp 、rsync 、Xshell 、VS Code Remote 都能用，用公钥登录，权限和网页里是同一套。 **网域网关**：机器在另一个机房、或者在公司 NAT 后面，Casvisor 直连不到时，用一个 SSH 跳板机中转；连跳板机都没有的网络，可以在里面随便找台机器跑 `casvisor agent`，它主动连出来，不监听端口。 密码和私钥都是加密存库的，SSH 主机密钥和 RDP 证书首次连接时记下来，之后变了就拒绝连接。用户全程看不到服务器的密码。 ### 控制 权限按 用户 / 用户组 × 资产 / 资产标签 来配，动作有连接、复制、粘贴、上传、下载、端口转发，可以限来源 IP 段和有效期。用的是 Casbin 。 命令规则：正则匹配，命中就拦（不把回车发给目标机器，改发 Ctrl+C ）或只告警。网页终端和 SSH 网关都生效。 撤销立即生效：改权限、删权限、权限到期，已经连着的会话会被断开。 ### 审计 四种协议的会话都录像，回放就在浏览器里，用的是实时连接那套代码。SSH 和 Telnet 的录像还能下载成 asciicast 。 在线会话可以实时旁观，也可以直接断掉。 SSH/Telnet 的命令记录是从一个虚拟屏幕里读的，Tab 补全、上箭头调历史、中文、行内编辑都能记准； vi 、top 这种全屏程序里的回车和输密码不记。 文件传输和所有 API 改动都在操作日志里。 ### 运维 顺带做了补丁管理：SSH 资产可以扫描待装的系统更新，一键安装、重启。Windows 走 Windows Update 的 COM 接口，Linux 支持 apt / dnf / yum 。 ### 部署 ```shell docker run -d --name casvisor -p 19000:19000 -p 2222:2222 \ -v casvisor-db:/db -v casvisor-recordings:/recordings casbin/casvisor ``` 默认 SQLite + 自带账号，管理员口令打印在日志里，第一次登录后改掉。要 SSO 、MFA 、LDAP 、社交登录，接 Casdoor 就行； Casdoor 的用户组直接能用在权限里。 ### 老实说的部分 - 没有数据库代理（ MySQL / PostgreSQL 的网页连接和 SQL 审计）和 K8s ，JumpServer 社区版这两个都有； - 一个资产只有一组系统账号，没有多账号、自动改密、访问申请工单； - 没有资产树和批量导入，资产多了管理起来比较笨； - 录像只能存在本机目录，还不能放 S3 / OSS ； - 本地账号模式没有 MFA ，要 MFA 得接 Casdoor ； - 命令审计靠读虚拟屏幕，不是把键盘输入全录下来，全屏程序里的操作看不到。 在线演示： https://demo.casvisor.com （有一个假的 SSH 和一个假的 VNC 可以连） 文档： https://casvisor.org 代码： https://github.com/casvisor/casvisor Apache-2.0 ，欢迎 issue 和 PR 。

projects.title: Show HN: Bot-bottle – secure runtime, DLP and remote control for local agents
projects.author: didericis
projects.summary: Hey! About 6 months ago, I started looking for a tool to safely run coding agents on my (security sensitive) developer machine. Specifically, I wanted a tool that: - I could use regardless of the model or harness running underneath - I could build simple, composable, plaintext security policies for - Provided strong vm level isolation - Hid credentials from agents - Scanned and monitored everything going in and out of agent workspace - Allowed me to use the same mobile flow I had gotten used to with claude code, but with arbitrary harnesses I couldn't find a tool that met all of these, so I started bot-bottle. It's evolved into what I'm hoping will be the best security conscious, local first coding agent orchestrator out there. Here's how it works: Each agent runs in its own microVM (Firecracker on Linux, Apple's container on macOS, Docker as a weaker fallback), with whichever harness you want. Claude Code, Codex and pi are built in, and custom agent providers are supported (still being documented/tested). What an agent can reach is defined in a "bottle", which is just a short markdown file listing hosts, repos and which secret goes to which host. Bottles are enforced by a gateway outside the agent VM, which adds the real credentials to requests on the way out, so the agent only sees placeholders. Bottles stack, so you can keep small ones around (npm read only, one repo, one API, etc) and combine them per task. Repos can ship their own bottles, which only run after you trust their exact contents. Outgoing requests and git pushes are scanned for secrets, and everything is logged locally (you can stream it to your own endpoint as NDJSON or OCSF). Anything a bottle doesn't allow comes to you for approval, in the terminal or on your phone through an optional paired console. It's in alpha (the console especially), so UI polish is still in progress. Install: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/diderisoft/bot-bottle/main/install.sh | sh Docs: https://bot-bottle.com/docs Would love feedback, especially on the threat model and on whether bottles are the right abstraction.

projects.title: Show HN: Ramble – Message your agent directly from your Apple Watch
projects.author: Jpoliachik
projects.summary: I made Ramble because I wanted to get off my phone but still be able to capture thoughts, reminders, action items - whatever. Some of my best thoughts happen when I'm playing with my kids or on a run - and this lets me stay in the moment, fire off a quick message on my watch and not get pulled into the screen waiting for AI to respond - never get sucked into 'lets solve this now' mindset. Ramble is designed for Apple Watch & offline first - to capture voice quickly and queue up messages to send when it can. The slim relay backend uses cloud transcription (Grok Whisper currently), then holds the message in an inbox for your agent to pickup and process, then gets purged from the backend after acknowledgement. No accounts, no signups. It uses Apple's App Attest for endpoint security. It works great with current gen personal agents like Muse, GrokBot, etc. (GrokBot supports incoming webhooks so its instant. Muse doesn't, so it polls every couple minutes (without waking the agent)) The linking process is surprisingly easy. Would love to hear what you think!

projects.title: Show HN: Vaultbase – a self-hosted back end in a single binary
projects.author: khalidsheet
projects.summary: One binary to run and you have a full backend at your fingertips: a database with a REST API, sign-in, realtime, files, server-side hooks and jobs, on SQLite or Postgres. It's MIT licensed. You can try the demo at https://demo.vaultbase.sh (the login is filled in, and it resets every hour). I built it to ship fast. I always tend to write the same logic for any new project, whether it's a side project or a small to medium project for a client. I wanted something my friends and I could work with fast, try new things with, and that's easy to use. Then it became something I really wanted to work on and make as complete as I can for any type of backend. As of writing this post it has 80 releases since May this year and is backed by more than 2,800 tests. I also run security reviews with Claude and fix what they find. It hasn't had an outside audit yet. It was built with the help of Claude, from the codebase to the documentation and fact-checking it against the code. Claude helped speed up the pace, find bugs, and write tests. Vaultbase is pre-1.0, so expect some bugs and issues here and there. I'm working hard to fix each and every one of them. Thank you for taking the time to read this. I'd really appreciate any feedback, even if you didn't like Vaultbase. The demo is yours to try, and it's two commands to run locally.

projects.title: Show HN: Beam – Pairing machines with passkeys; replace SSH&VPN's with Tailcat
projects.author: hermannbjorgvin
projects.summary: A concept I wanted to share that is built on TailScale's Tailcat https://tailscale.com/tailcat The inspiration is that I was thinking of ways to allow my users to be able to pool their machines easily without needing to set up SSH or a VPN. How can you lower the barrier to entry without compromising on security. The end result is you get a remote shell connection and a Tailcat tunnel that only requires your user to know how to use passkeys to verify their machines. Any machine can join the pool without having connected to the others at any point before which is also a strength. The primary weakness is that even though all the passkey assertion and encryption/decryption happens on the browser side you are still trusting a Cloudflare worker to store it. So I think this is more of a solution for things like Herdr, T3 code, etc etc where you want to connect machines in a pool. Each machine also has a small SQLite mail inbox for those purposes, you can queue messages that your machine will receive next time it is reachable. For a more in depth explanation I created this artifact with Fable 5.2 and Astra 6 to clean up the prose: https://claude.ai/artifact/NVHSV1FNmpPaPsqRakskVW

projects.title: [开源推荐] AgentFlow：Docker 一键私有化部署的 AI Agent 平台
projects.author: PHclaw

github.name: PHclaw/agentflow
github.description: 自托管 AI Agent 平台：拖拽式工作流 + 知识库 RAG + 23 个预置技能，默认 SQLite 单机可跑，一条 docker compose 私有化部署。Self-hosted, OpenAI-compatible.

projects.summary: 一个自托管的 AI Agent 平台：在浏览器里拖拽连几个节点、填几行提示词，就能把大模型、内部文档和常用工具拼成能干活儿的助手。默认两个容器加一个 SQLite 文件，不依赖 PostgreSQL 和 Redis，一条 docker compose 命令跑起来，数据存在自己硬盘上。适合数据不能出内网、又没有专职运维的中小团队；代码量适中，也适合拿来读源码。 亮点 1. 部署成本低到能塞进一台小机器 两个容器（后端 + nginx）加一个 ./data/agentflow.db 就是全部，docker compose up -d --build 完成部署，备份等于打包 data/ 目录。同类自托管方案起步通常要 PostgreSQL + Redis + worker，四五个容器。 2. 产物是真文件，不是一段文字 生成的 xlsx / png / pdf 作为附件回传，图片类直接内联渲染在对话里，不用先下载再看。这一点和多数「只回文本」的方案差别明显。 3. 换模型不用重启，已入库的向量也不会失效 任意 OpenAI 兼容端点（含本地 Ollama），界面里保存即生效。embedding 端点独立配置——换对话模型不影响向量库，不用重新入库。很多同类产品把这两个绑在一起，换模型等于重建知识库。 4. 技能就是目录 加一个带 SKILL.md 的文件夹就多一个能力，仓库自带 26 个（Excel 表格、PPT 生成、PDF 处理、学术检索、会议纪要、统计分析…），扩展不需要改任何代码。 5. 工作流引擎自研，节点状态实时回传 没有用 LangGraph——需求就六类节点（触发器 / LLM / 知识库 / 工具 / 条件 / 回复），引框架反而多一层调试成本。自研的好处是画布上的节点会逐个点亮，用户能看见跑到哪一步。 适合初学者学什么 后端 FastAPI + SQLAlchemy 2.0 async，前端 React 18 + ReactFlow，代码量适中，读源码能学到几条完整链路： SSE 流式输出：为什么不用 EventSource（不能带 Authorization 头），改用 fetch + ReadableStream 后怎么按帧解析 向量检索落地：文档解析 → 分块 → 调 embedding 端点 → 存 chromadb → 检索注入上下文，一整条 RAG 链路 把 LLM 应用做成可部署产品：Alembic 迁移与 createall 的顺序坑、JWT 鉴权、限流、Docker 多阶段构建 原生打包：用 Capacitor 把同一个 Web 前端打成安卓 App，下载逻辑怎么从 换成 Filesystem + Share 已知限制 没有异步任务队列（长任务会占住请求），权限只有「用户 / 管理员」两档，pgvector 路径未做端到端验证。定位是小团队自用，不适合高并发场景。

projects.summary: 我做了一个工具：3 分钟就能把 GPT 生成的图片转成可编辑的 PPT，艺术字也能保留。 之前做汇报 PPT 时，我发现 AI 生成的幻灯片非常好看，是我这种理科生远远做不出来的。问题是它改不了。AI 只要出现一点小幻觉，或者文案有点 AI 味，就只能重新生成、反复抽卡，结果还不一定比第一次好，让人很恼火😡。我也试过不少 skill，烧了一堆 token，速度和效果都不理想，所以决定自己做一个转换工具。 传送门：https://editableppt.com/ 在这之前，我试过 gpt-image-2.5 的透明背景、Seedream5、Canva、Codia，还去闲鱼找过代做。代做明码标价，一页 1～2 元，偏贵。而且我发现他们用的也是 Canva 或 Codia，做得还没有我自己精细。 转了一圈，我发现现在的做法大致分两派： - **基于生图模型**：先标注并抠出可拆分的元素，再用 OCR 提取文字，最后重新生成背景。优点是可控；缺点是成本高、速度慢，背景补全全靠运气，文字一多就补不好。它也很难处理多层结构，一般只能拆两层，层数一多就更慢，成本也直线上升。 - **Canva 路线**：要自己部署分割模型、inpainting 模型、OpenCV 和 OCR 深度模型，普通人很难负担。而且 Canva 识别中文效果差，容易乱码，大段文本还会丢失格式。 于是我想把两者结合起来：在现有 GPT 模型和一些开源模型的基础上做微调，再拿大量案例让 Claude 反复测试效果。最后真的做成了，目前在我测试的产品里，我做的是最精细的，该转的转，不该转的不转，特别对中文进行了优化，段落换行和中文识别。 我自己的问题解决了，相信别人也会遇到同样的困扰，所以做了这个网站，希望能帮到同样被做 PPT 困扰的人。 我给大家准备了免费试用积分，不够用可以私聊我。遇到问题、发现 bug 或者想要新功能，都可以直接回复或发邮件给我。 ![预览图](https://i.imgur.com/rQXNnHZ.jpeg)

projects.title: Show HN: Darkroomfinder.org – A Directory of Photography Darkrooms
projects.author: stokesj84
projects.summary: I built darkroomfinder.org, a directory of photography darkrooms, as a React single page app (SPA), because I wanted to understand how SPAs work and I wanted to scale to hundreds or thousands of cities without managing routes and pages for each of them. The site currently lists over 350 darkrooms across over 50 countries. However in deciding to build a SPA I failed to realize the downsides of SPAs for SEO. As an SPA darkroomfinder.org only has one route, i.e. darkroomfinder.org. Therefore GoogleBot only indexes the root domain and if someone searches for "Darkrooms" the site might surface in Google Search, but if a user searches "San Francisco Darkrooms" Google Search is much less likely to return darkroomfinder.org as nothing indicates the site has information about San Francisco. Solving this SEO problem while maintaining the simplicity of the SPA turned out to be a challenge but I think I have arrived at a solution that checks most of the desired boxes at the cost of being tied more closely to Cloudflare's infrastructure. Cloudflare, the DNS and CDN for darkroomfinder.org, has a serverless primitive, Cloudflare Workers. These Cloudflare Workers are distributed at the edge, have KV caches, and can intercept specific paths. So my solution to having both an SPA and indexable city routes is to have Cloudflare Workers cache the city data and intercept city routes directed at darkroomfinder.org returning an HTML page with the city data and the full React SPA which boots over the HTML page. So technically it's one SPA served to many routes. GoogleBot in traversing one of these city routes, like darkroomfinder.org/san-francisco, will index the HTML page while humans using browsers receive the same HTML which the React SPA boots over. Part of the project that remains unsolved is data collection and validation. Darkroom discovery is automated by agents running daily scans for unlisted darkrooms. But a human still has to validate that the discovered darkrooms exist and try to determine what capabilities they have such as B&W or color developing etc. I am currently working on an automated reachability and vitality checker to determine if the darkrooms already in the directory are still active, since photography darkrooms sometimes cease operations long before taking down their websites or social feeds. darkroomfinder.org

projects.author: zkitkevin
projects.summary: 最近在尝试做英文游戏攻略站，刚把一个围绕 Suzy Says 的小站上线： https://suzysays.co/ Suzy Says 是 MOONBIT 做的一款恐怖游戏。我这边做的是非官方攻略站，主要整理官方下载入口、新手说明和结局相关资料。 这次用了 AI 配合网站引擎，从查搜索结果、确定页面内容，到写页面、预览和发布，完整走了一遍。 过程中有两件事让我印象比较深。 一开始想做成首页直接玩的游戏站，但核实后发现，作者官方提供的是 Windows 下载版。网上虽然有些页面写着“在线玩 Suzy Says”，继续查它实际加载的游戏地址，却发现其中一个嵌入的是另一款游戏。所以最后改成了攻略和官方下载指引，没有硬塞一个播放器进去。 另一个是结局资料。不同视频和攻略对 Good、True、Bad 的叫法不完全一致，有些触发条件也互相矛盾。现在的处理方式是把开发者明确确认的信息和视频作者的说法分开，附上来源，不把没验证过的步骤写成确定的通关教程。 目前主要做了三个页面： - 首页：官方下载入口、操作和版本区别。 - 新手指南：尽量不剧透，给第一次玩的人看。 - 结局参考：整理名称差异、Full 版要求和相关视频，剧透提示可以展开。 站点部署在 Cloudflare Workers 上，页面通过引擎生成，支持预览后再发布。中间还遇到一个引擎检查默认要求首页必须绑定游戏的问题，后来补了攻略首页模式才顺利上线。 想请大家帮忙看看几个地方： 1. 第一眼能不能看懂这是一个什么站？ 2. 页面导航和文章入口是否好找？ 3. 如果你是搜这个游戏进来的，还希望看到什么内容？ 英文表达、页面体验或者资料准确性有问题，也欢迎直接指出来

projects.author: hzbd

github.name: schiplat/signet
github.description: Lightweight unified identity authentication (SSO / OIDC IdP) service

projects.summary: Signet 是用 Rust 编写的统一身份认证服务，定位为组织内的 OIDC Identity Provider（IdP），为多个内部子系统提供标准 SSO 登录能力。 设计目标是「轻量、可自托管、协议标准」，而不是做成功能庞杂的企业级 IAM 全家桶。 核心特点： Rust 单二进制部署：Release 提供 linux-amd64 / linux-arm64 / macos-arm64 自包含二进制，Dashboard 在编译期嵌入，只需一个 PostgreSQL 即可运行（数据库迁移也内置，启动自动执行）。也支持 Docker 镜像。 标准 OIDC：支持 authorize / token / PKCE / refresh / userinfo / JWKS / endsession / revoke 等端点。 完整管理后台：用户与组织树（部门/组）、客户端管理、审计日志、MFA（TOTP）、Passkey、运行时策略配置、品牌定制（Logo/产品名）等。 自助能力：普通用户可在「My apps」自助注册自己的 OAuth 客户端；管理员仍有全局管控。 第三方登录（身份联邦）：已支持 GitHub、Google、飞书、微信开放平台以及通用 OIDC。 集成扩展：RFC 7591 动态客户端注册、Webhooks（含飞书卡片）、SCIM v2 目录同步、LDAP / HTTP JSON 目录同步等。 运维友好：会话/Token 有效期、登录锁定、密码策略、限流等均可在后台热修改，无需重启；支持签名密钥轮换。 适合中小团队、内网多系统、个人/小团队自建 SSO 的场景。如果觉得 Keycloak、Authentik 等太重，又想要标准 OIDC + 现代 Dashboard，可以试一下 Signet。 文档比较完整（中英文），有设计说明、安全说明、客户端接入指南和示例（Axum OIDC Client）。 欢迎试用和反馈。

projects.summary: # DocuKit — 在浏览器里把文档转成图片 **PDF / Word 转 PNG、JPG，全程在你的浏览器标签页里完成。不上传、不注册、无水印，最高 600 DPI。** ## 为什么做它 投简历的时候，招聘平台和 HR 经常要求把简历转成 PNG 或 JPG。截图发过去糊得看不清，WPS 导出图片要另外收费，各种在线转换站又要求先上传文件、排队、看广告 同样的情况反复发生了几次，我意识到缺的不是"转换功能"，而是一个**不用上传、打开就能用**的工具。 ## 主要功能 - **PDF → PNG / JPG**：基于 pdf.js 在本地渲染，30 页的文档也不用等服务器 - **DOCX → PNG / JPG**：还原 Word 排版后按页切片，尽量贴近原件观感 - **96 / 150 / 300 / 600 四档 DPI** + JPG 质量滑杆，屏幕阅读到印刷输出都覆盖 - **多页合并长图**：竖排或横排拼接，自动裁掉页边距白边，可设置间距 - **批量处理**：多文件一次转换，逐张下载或整体打包 ZIP，结果支持预览、复制到剪贴板 ## 技术要点 - 纯前端实现，PDF 走原生渲染、DOCX 走排版后截图两条路线 - Word 在浏览器里没有固定分页，按内容高度动态切片，让页数和 Word 保持一致 - 600 DPI 下按画布像素上限动态降采样，在清晰度和内存之间取平衡 - 中英双语、按页更新进度、额度用尽时自动回退本地转换 - 部署在 Cloudflare Pages，配了站点地图、双语 hreflang 和 IndexNow ## 使用与边界 打开 https://docukit.win 拖入文件即可，无需注册、无需邀请码。 已知限制：Word 仅支持 .docx，单文件上限 200 MB；复杂分栏、文本框、页眉页脚的还原可能与 Word 有偏差，纯文字和简单表格最稳。另外有一个可选的「高保真模式」会把文件发送到第三方服务处理，默认关闭，处理敏感文件时请保持关闭。 **在线体验：** https://docukit.win

projects.title: 【开源自荐】zniff：Rust + NSH 构建的原生 HTTP(S) 抓包调试工具
projects.author: vicanso
projects.summary: zniff 是一款基于纯 Rust 编写的轻量级 HTTP(S) 抓包与调试代理工具，界面使用原生跨平台 UI 框架 NSH 构建。整个代理内核与 GUI 窗口编译为单个二进制文件，告别高内存占用和卡顿，带来启动迅速、原生流畅的桌面抓包体验；同时同一套界面代码还可编译为 WebAssembly，通过 zniff --web 或 Docker 一键部署为团队/远程网页控制台。 ────── 核心特性一览 🚀 原生轻量，单二进制开箱即用：不依赖外部运行时与数据库，代理内核与界面同进程运行，支持深浅双色自适应主题、列宽/列序拖拽记忆、窗口尺寸持久化与流式大正文磁盘溢出缓存， 长时间高并发抓包依然保持低内存与流畅滚动。 🧩 严格协议跟随与全链路透视： • HTTP/1.1 & HTTP/2 多路复用：直接解析 TLS ClientHello 的 ALPN 提案并与源站协商，不降级为 HTTP/1.1。 • WebSocket（RFC 6455）与 SSE：完整记录双向帧与流式事件，支持按方向、帧类型与关键字实时过滤并单帧复制。 • 连接阶段耗时拆解：清晰展示 DNS、TCP、TLS 握手与连接复用状态，超过 1 秒慢请求自动高亮提示。 • 证书与移动端一键接入：macOS 一键导入并信任系统钥匙串，支持直接为运行中的 iOS 模拟器配置证书与代理；内置二维码安装页，手机扫码即可配置真机抓包。 🔍 请求与响应深度洞察： • 多格式智能解码：JSON（含可折叠、可搜索的树形视图）、GraphQL（自动拆分 operationName、查询语句与变量）、HTML/Markdown 实时渲染预览、XML、无模式 Protobuf/gRPC Wire 解码与 MessagePack 转 JSON。 • 行内自动识别：JWT、Unix 时间戳、可打印 Base64 自动在原值下方解码提示；十六进制视图支持 16/32 字节自适应排布与行号剥离复制。 • 基准对比与检索：支持将任意请求设为基准进行行级 Diff 对比，支持请求/响应正文内实时搜索高亮，以及一键生成瀑布图、泳道时序图、依赖流转图和 Mermaid 源码。 🛠️ 15 项改写规则、断点队列与高效重放： • 15 种规则开箱即用：覆盖 map-local（支持单文件、目录映射与回源）、map-remote、break、break-res、block、replace、json（JSON Path 改写）、delay、throttle、header、query、cors、no-cache、cert（自定义域名证书/mTLS 客户端证书）与 resolve（自定义 Host/IP 解析），支持 GraphQL op= 精准匹配与多配置方案导出/拖拽导入。 • 8 槽位 FIFO 断点与编辑重发：支持请求/响应双侧断点拦截、直接粘贴 cURL 自动解析填充、编辑后放行或丢弃，以及并发批量重放。 • 丰富过滤与多语言导出：支持 host:、path:、op:、body:、header:、slow:、pin: 与 - 反向过滤及分面快速筛选；一键导出 cURL、fetch、Python requests、Rust reqwest、Go net/http、TypeScript 接口定义与 Rust serde 结构体。 🤖 AI 原生 MCP 与团队分享： • 内置 MCP Server：原生支持 JSON-RPC 2.0 MCP 协议（POST /mcp 与 zniff --mcp），Claude Desktop、Cursor 等客户端可直接查询会话列表、读取流量详情、添加备注、重放请求或读写抓包规则。 • 脱敏导出与实时分享：支持 HAR / 单文件 HTML 快照导出（可选敏感字段脱敏预览），并可通过 /s/{uuid} 分享实时抓包会话或配合 zniff --relay 中转访问。 💻 全平台支持与私有化部署：支持 macOS（已签名 .dmg，支持应用内静默更新与自动重启）、Windows 与 Linux（提供一键安装脚本），同时提供 vicanso/zniff-web Docker 镜像支持私有化 Web 控制台与中继部署，抓包端口、Web 控制台与中继服务均支持独立认证保护。

projects.title: Show HN: DownForReal – Kuma Hosted from 3 regions
projects.author: hodder
projects.summary: I use Kuma for a few microservices I’ve built. It’s a simple open source tool for monitoring APIs, ports, websites etc if they are down. The issue I get is that they are hosted on your own infrastructure, so it doesn’t do you a whole lot of good if your site is down and it takes your Kuma down with it. This also leads to a bunch of false notifications which are annoying. From what I can tell, people in the GitHub comments are looking for hosted Kuma. I built DownForReal (largely with LLMs) but what it does is it hosts Kuma and if Kuma is reporting the service down, probes from US, Frankfurt, and Singapore are sent to confirm the outage (looking for 2 out of 3 of the regions). I’m asking $10 a month or $75 a year. I’m really just launching this as a service bc I built it for myself. There is also a simple importer for uptimerobot exports.

projects.title: Show HN: a Rust implementation of the Reticulum mesh networking stack

projects.summary: This is a fork of original rust sdk from https://github.com/BeechatNetworkSystemsLtd/Reticulum-rs/ that I extended significantly to make it fully feature compatible with the reference implementation that is built in python. I wanted to expand the rust sdk to give me full toolbox and easy way to do bindings for different languages including for building mobile apps. it covers the full surface: pathfinding and announce propagation, links, requests, resource transfers(bzip2, same wire format), identity ratchets, tunnels, LXMF messaging with propagation sync, serial/KISS/AX.25, RNode (incl. BLE), IPv6 auto-peering and I2P interfaces, Kotlin and Swift bindings so mobile apps can embed the stack directly. CLI tools (rnstatus, rnpath, rnsh, rnx) are ported too. I've done some experiments with it liek creating a LoRa chat firmware for the M5Stack Cardputer and a full node/repeater for M5Stack Unit C6L to have a tiny reticulum node with full stack Before anyone gives me shit - I've opened an upstream PR but given the size of the change I'dnt blame them for not wanting to deal with it.

projects.title: [开源推荐] Folio：本地优先的 Windows + Android 双端阅读器
projects.author: flulwh

github.name: flulwh/folio
github.description: 极简沉浸式电子书阅读器：Electron + React 桌面端 + Kotlin/Compose Android 客户端，局域网同步阅读进度与痕迹

projects.summary: Folio 是我自己每天在用的阅读器：桌面端 Electron + React，安卓端是原生 Kotlin + Jetpack Compose。它只把「读一本书」这件事做干净——书架就是首页，点开即读，工具栏随滚动淡出；进度按段落锚定，换字号、换栏宽之后仍回到原来那一句。两端不需要账号，同一 Wi-Fi 下桌面端开一个只监听内网的 HTTP 服务，手机填地址加 6 位访问码即可接入，阅读进度、书签、划线、笔记双向同步。没有云端、没有中转、不托管任何内容。 亮点 为长文阅读打磨的排版 虚拟滚动：几十万段的长篇只渲染视口附近的段落，滚动不掉帧；段落高度按「书 + 排版 + 栏宽」缓存到 localStorage（Uint16 + base64，长篇也存得下），第二次打开直接命中，不再整本重排。 中文排印细节：text-wrap: pretty 处理尾行孤字、hanging-punctuation 让句读悬挂、palt 收紧标点；字号、行距、栏宽、段距、首行缩进、字体族都能调，也能装自己的 ttf/otf/woff2（安装时就告诉你含不含中文）。 正则章节识别：「第X章 / Chapter N / 序章 / 楔子 / 【标题】」开箱可用，也能在设置里写自己的正则；目录支持章节搜索与当前章高亮。 痕迹按段落锚定：书签、划线、笔记在换字号、换栏宽后不会错位；页边一道朱砂短竖线标记书签。 自动滚动四档速度（15/25/40/60 px/s），[ ] 随时调速，滚轮一碰立刻交回手感。 双端同步：只走局域网，不上云 桌面端只用 Node 内置 http 起面板，零依赖、不增加打包体积，只监听内网；6 位访问码可一键更换。 同步阅读进度、书签、划线、笔记与书源配置；冲突按 updatedAt 新者胜、字段浅合并，不打断两边正在进行的滚动。 手机浏览器也能直接读：本地书自动切章节目录，云端书的目录与正文由本机书源引擎现抓，翻章、拖进度条都能用。 断网不丢：顶部明说「有一处进度还没同步」，联网后自动补写；也可以关掉写入权限，让面板退化成纯看板。 原生安卓端，不是 WebView 套壳 Kotlin + Compose + Miuix（HyperOS 风格），阅读控制层是浮动圆角卡片，不挤压正文。 点正文两侧或按音量键翻页，到章末自动接下一章；本地书正文下到手机私有目录，锁屏、飞行模式都能读。 省电：没有前台服务、没有常驻通知、不轮询，阅读页只组合可见段落。 APK 约 12 MB，minSdk 26；版本线与桌面端独立（桌面 2.x / 安卓 3.x），可分开升级。 书源与边界 兼容「阅读」(Legado) 书源：订阅链接（legado://import/…）、本地 JSON、粘贴 JSON 都能导入；书源仓库可按单条 / 本页 / 整批导入，试搜结果按健康度排序，一键筛掉失效源。 云端阅读按 3 章一个窗口并行抓取，读到底自动续接；失败章节标占位、可一键重试，阅读位置不丢。 不内置书城、不代理、不托管内容：书源只是解析规则，正文只在用户机器与源站之间流动。 MIT；books.json / progress.json / marks.json 字段双端对齐，变更保持向前兼容。 截图或演示视频 桌面端： 安卓端： 更多截图（目录、自动滚动、书籍市场、深色主题、设置页）见 README： 快速开始 Windows 10/11 x64：在 Releases 下载 Folio-Setup-2.9.2.exe（推荐）或单文件便携版，双击即用，不写注册表。 Android 8.0+：下载 Folio-3.5.0 APK。 源码运行：桌面端 npm install && npm run dev（Vite 热更新 + Electron 窗口）；安卓端 cd android && ./gradlew assembleDebug。 先看效果：装好后书架是空的，点「读示例《山居手记》」即可进入沉浸阅读。 连手机：桌面端 设置 → 网络 → 开启面板；手机 设置 → 桌面端连接 填地址和访问码，或点「搜索桌面端」。 适合谁 想把 TXT / Markdown 和阅读记录留在自己机器上，又需要在电脑和手机之间接着读的人。 已经在用 Legado 书源、希望桌面端也有同等阅读体验的人。 不适合：需要在线书城、云端书架、公网多设备同步的场景。

projects.title: Show HN: Every Satellite in Orbit Since 1957
projects.author: daedbe
projects.summary: I originally built this visualisation of the GCAT ( https://planet4589.org/space/gcat/ ) database a few years ago as part of some university coursework. It then sat collecting dust for a while, but I've finally found the time to give it a bit of a visual overhaul. It's now something I'm happy to share. The main motivation with creating this was to show two things: just how much stuff is currently orbiting Earth, and how dramatically that number has increased over the last few years. Speaking to some friends about this, we agreed that it's easy to read statistics about how many satellites there are, but it's hard to put those numbers into perspective. Visualising this from space and seeing everything orbiting our planet at once really drives home the scale of it!

projects.title: Show HN: A browser RTS where you play alongside your local agents
projects.author: fraywing
projects.summary: Howdy HN! Inspired by StarSkirmish, I wanted to build a complex RTS that required you to bring your OWN agents and either play with them as allies, against them as enemies, or battle head-to-head with other agent-human pairs in public matches. In AC you operate one or more planes (Orbit, Sky, Surface, Depths) of differing gameplay. As an old-school PC gamer I wanted the mechanics to resemble some of my favorite 90s games of yore: C&C, DungeonKeeper, Homeworld, StarCraft, and others. The idea is that you have specific objectives needed to maximize resource generation, aid in cross player support, and that a single plane cannot win independently. Outside of gameplay, from an agentic tech pov, there are some other really cool things that come with this, including: - A full specification + library to install agents into any game ( http://playerthree.gg/ ) - A networking SDK for bidirectional agent communication - Symmetric maps - Deterministic simulation - Benchmarking tools - (soon) published benchmark data Github: https://github.com/agent-command/agent-command Play now: https://agentcommand.gg/ Would love feedback and contribs if interested in RTS games and AI!

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Zorven：一条命令把本机服务发布到公网 HTTPS 的开源内网穿透工具
projects.author: MARRY45

projects.author: bromney
projects.summary: Site URL: https://fmrl.live Repository URL: https://gitlab.com/croatoa/fmrl This project allows you to host a website, content, and streaming from an open browser window. It gets served over WebRTC connections (or a Cloudfare turn server if that's not available). This is just a start. Any suggestions or feedback to improve usability, feature requests, etc is super welcome. This is a project I've had in mind for a while. I wanted to participate in building for a decentralized web, so I thought it would be cool if people could run a social network kind of page from their own machine, and allow them to diffuse content over a peer to peer net, independent of the typical social media giants. While this iteration is not quite that, it's a start. While the UI probably makes this super obvious, this is the first time I've used AI in coding (LLM, Claude Code). It really is some impressive machinery. The goal isn't privacy, but rather autonomy, more or less. I know there are real limitations (like a host user closing their browser) but I feel like the idea is at least slightly novel (probably because its a mediocre idea lol).. but it'll be interesting to see how it evolves. If you made it this far, thanks for the read. Hope you have a pleasant day.

projects.title: 【工具自荐】Ampuly Engine：可本地部署的 Agent 项目与业务协作引擎（源码预览）

projects.summary: 大家好，我们是 Ampuly 团队，自荐一个正在征集开发者反馈的源码预览项目。 项目： Ampuly Engine / 安普里引擎 说明： 中文 README · English README 它做什么 Ampuly Engine 是面向项目任务与业务协作的 Python 引擎，包含 Agent 执行、工具调用、审批、项目数据和浏览器控制台源码，可在本地部署。 我们想探索的问题是：在一个本地项目环境里组织 Agent、任务和审批，能否减少团队协作中的配置与交接成本？这次先开放通用引擎供开发者评估，私有业务流、客户数据和账号信息均不包含在公开仓库内。早期基础来自 HKUDS/OpenOPC，已保留来源与第三方许可说明。 适合谁，以及当前进度 适合愿意自行准备 Python/Node 环境、从合成数据开始评估的开发者。在新建 Windows 环境中，依赖安装、前端/wheel 构建，以及控制台建号、登录、创建/列出空白项目的基础流程已通过检查。 仍是开发者源码预览，整体尚未验收通过。 不附带一键安装器；真实模型/外部 Agent 完整流程、生产业务流程、浏览器端到端交互和第二台实体电脑安装尚未验证。后台用户配置发现及安装进程退出还有已记录的限制，详情写在 README，不建议直接接入生产资料。 许可说明 本项目是源码可见、附条件商用，不是 OSI 批准的开源许可。适用原创部分的商用需要书面授权：共享方案允许安普里仅为内部研究和产品改进使用有权提供的脱敏业务流设计；保密方案按引擎直接交付产生的实收收入扣除退款及代收税费后计收 3%。两种方案按明确约定申报必要收入汇总，安装不会自动上传业务流或收入。完整边界见 LICENSE，上游及第三方权利不变。 我们尤其希望收集干净环境安装、项目/任务组织、审批和执行边界方面的反馈。欢迎通过仓库 Discussions 交流，或提交可复现且脱敏的 Issue。感谢审阅。

projects.title: 做了个 Mac 小工具，合 MR 之前就能看出 GitLab pipeline 会不会出问题
projects.author: wddwycc
projects.summary: 做了个 Mac 小工具 Pipeline Lens ，在本地模拟 GitLab CI pipeline 。 项目稍微大一点，.gitlab-ci.yml 就会拆成一堆 include ，再加上 rules 、needs 、extends 、!reference ，改 CI 配置的时候心里很没底。MR 自己的 pipeline 推上去跑一遍就知道了，问题是它只验证 MR 自己：合进去之后 main 、release 分支、tag 上的 pipeline 会变成什么样，合之前谁也不知道。 比如给 `build-api` 加了个 `changes: [api/**/*]`，想省点 CI 时间。MR 全绿，合进去之后 release 分支上 `deploy-production` 还 needs 它，GitLab 直接不给建 pipeline ，发版那天才发现。 Pipeline Lens 会把 include （本地、跨项目、通配符）都拉下来合并，然后模拟任意分支、tag 或 MR 的 pipeline：会跑哪些 job 、每个 job 是哪条 rule 决定的、没跑的为啥没跑（连用到的变量值都列出来），以及 GitLab 会因为什么报错拒绝建这条 pipeline 。上面那种情况，用 Config from 拿 MR 分支的配置去模拟 release 分支，合之前就能看出来。gitlab-org/gitlab 这种大规模的项目也能模拟。 免费，macOS 14+ 就能装： * [App Store]( https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6827171674?pt=119022345&ct=v2ex&mt=8) * [更多介绍]( https://monk-studio.com/pipeline-lens) 有配置模拟出来跟 GitLab 实际不一样的，欢迎扔过来，我修。

projects.title: Show HN: Kapso – Iterative learning from enterprise data
projects.author: alirezamshi
projects.summary: Hey HN! We're Alireza and Majid building Leeroo ( https://leeroo.com/ ). Previously we’ve built AI systems for products with millions of users, including at LinkedIn and Meta. We’re now focusing on building AI systems for enterprise data. Today, we're open-sourcing Kapso ( https://github.com/Leeroo-AI/kapso ), an engine that runs experiments, deploys the best solution, and learns from every run. The nature of data work is iterative: investigate, form hypotheses, experiment, and improve based on what you learn. This bottom-up process is the only way to deliver meaningful outcomes quickly in large, messy enterprise data environments. Consultants gathering context in meetings or teams defining a business ontology upfront to fit into the data has no chance of execution, in quarters and sometimes years. An AI-native system should automate this process, compounding learning to each new investigation and implementation. For instance, one of our enterprise projects was moving a company off its old data estate onto a lakehouse with more than 30 source-system families, thousands of tables and transformations, and hundreds of BI reports. No individual or AI agent knew how that data estate was connected and operated. The only way to learn it was to investigate the company's repos, dbt models, documentation, and data itself and propose hypotheses about the estate, run experiments, and learn from them, until we understand how each system behaves and under which conditions. The iterative work goes beyond understanding how data and systems fit together, and the business operations. Building useful software is iterative too. Whether you’re optimizing a warehouse, building a lakehouse pipeline or predicting churn, you need to run experiments and learn what works best in that environment. As you deliver more projects, that know-how compounds, similar in principle to RL. RAGing documentation has little value until it has been tried in a specific environment and the consequences are learned. As with human engineering work, experimentation and learning should happen in a sandbox. We built Kapso for this kind of work, you give it an objective and success criteria, and it works towards an optimum solution that can be deployed on your stack. You can view a video walkthrough here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W4FHlza1fRs Here’s how it works… Kapso has a bank of lessons that are induced or deduced from the past experiments, and each carries a credence score, conditions on where it applies, and the evidence behind it. For each new experiment, an ideation module proposes ideas considering the earlier lessons, re-ranks them by expected return against the budget each would use, and sends the top-ranked ones to the implementor. Because the bank keeps learning from the past experiments in that environment, the proposed ideas are better suited to it than generic hypotheses from an LLM or RAG. Also, results of each experiment are verified by a verifier module that no experiment can access and cheat. As we’ve found when building such systems, sometimes the success criteria and evaluation tests need to be evolved. The experimentation modules can propose updates to the metrics and criteria for the verifier to approve or reject. After each run, learn() updates the bank of lessons’ scores and boundaries using the evidence from that run. Changes to the bank can also be A/B tested by running otherwise identical builds with the previous and updated banks. The bank is built on git, so you can share your experience with others, list the banks available to you, and update them (`kapso experience share/list/update` in CLI). The system is model-agnostic and coding-agent-agnostic. kapso.deploy(solution, target_stack) follows the same workflow, runs a shorter experimentation loop to adapt the best solution to the target stack (e.g. Docker, Modal, BentoCloud, LangGraph). Every domain has a harness to start from, you can write your own domain harness with /kapso:harness in the plugin or through CLI (kapso harness new <name>), and compound over that by running experimentations. We ran it on some public benchmarks and live competitions, with the following results… - Predictive modelling on relational databases: first on RelBench, Kumo AI (now Nvidia) and Stanford's benchmark, ahead of the best tabular foundation model ( https://star-project.stanford.edu/relbench/leaderboard/ ). This shows that keeping the learning in the harness-level can beat foundational table models. Updating a bank of lessons costs far less than retraining a tabular foundation model. - ML Engineering: First on OpenAI's MLE-bench at submission, still among the top open-source systems ( https://github.com/openai/mle-bench/pull/107 ). - AI competitions: ahead of the best agent the ALE-Bench authors at Sakana AI reported, and running autonomously at the live International Olympiad in AI 2026, above all 471 human contestants and in the top three AI systems ( https://ioai-official.org/ai-models-track/ioai%c2%b2-2026-re... ). We have a public bank for ML and Data at Leeroopedia ( https://leeroopedia.com/ ): around 100k pages extracted by experimenting on papers and repos, about 6M requests a month, about 28% from AI agents. If you are at a growing company with a complex data estate across multiple systems and functions, and your data and AI team is stretched, we would love to help! https://github.com/Leeroo-AI/kapso

projects.author: adriant93
projects.summary: I've been a developer for half my life now. I have a metric ton of projects which I've always had a hard time naming and juggling around, my stack has been the same for maybe 5 years now: - Gitkraken for git, along with its profiles to juggle between work, personal and open source - Termius for SSH connections that work on the mobile as well - Jetbrains Toolbox for quickly opening my projects in IDEs I lost my job in December 2025, and when the subscriptions bill came through, I saw it and I decided to build my own. So introducing: BranchBay and BranchShell pretty much. BranchBay is like Gitkraken on steroids - rust drawn, has tabs and groups for grouping repositories, pretty much like Chrome. You can pull tabs out and split into a new session. BranchShell is on mobile + desktop as well, it holds all your SSH, Databases, S3, Port forwarding connections in an encrypted vault locally. Best thing is the tray app which you can quickly press global shortcuts like Cmd+Ctrl+O, and see all the repositories you have, with their profiles, with the groups, and quickly either open it in your favorite IDE or terminal and work with them. Because I built them for myself, to get rid of my own subscriptions, I've decided to put them online for $20 one time payment for 2 machines. The goal is to basically help devs get out of this subscription hell and save some money in the age of AI. The programs have been out for a couple of months now, and I'm using them daily. I'm happy to add new features and take input on them. I wanna build something that actually helps devs both financially and workflow wise.

projects.title: 想听听你的想法！
projects.author: verylove
projects.summary: 先把身份说清楚，免得被当成广告号：白天上班，晚上回家改 bug 的一个人，没团队、没预算、没运营。这个小程序是自己做的，运行了也有 2、3 年了，现在还活着，也有人真在用。 发帖不是为了刷屏推广(有些友们已经用过，看过，见过)，就三个问题：它现在哪里不行、还缺什么、需要什么。 ## 它是什么 潮汐表表，一个微信小程序，查潮汐和天气的。 打开就是当前定位（也能手选城市）：一条潮汐曲线，涨落潮时间、潮高变化，上面一排天气——温度、风力风向、降雨概率。 3.0 版本加了个「去哪」：列附近能赶海、能钓鱼的点位。每个点标着特色（看日落、挖蛤蜊、抓螃蟹、钓鱼）、常出鱼种，能一键导航，能收藏，自己也能分享私藏的点。 不用下载，微信里搜「潮汐表表」就能打开，小程序码长这样： ![潮汐表表]( https://i.imgur.com/4Sjvp8I.jpeg) 看不到的链接: https://i.imgur.com/4Sjvp8I.jpeg ## 这两年听到的反馈，基本三类 1、界面丑。说实话我认。我的审美大概停在「能看懂就行」这一档，配色、字体、图表挤不挤，我自己已经看不出问题了，天天看的东西都麻木了（已经在进行中了，但是毕竟不是设计师~）。 2、广告多。现在是激励视频，主要是为了抵掉潮汐和天气接口的调用费和服务器费用，一年下来是笔真钱。但我理解有人就是不想看，这条我想听你们的为了免广告做了 VIP 可以减少广告影响体验(实验性质的)。 3、竞品一大堆。潮汐+、各种赶海小程序、天气 App 里自带的潮汐，我确实只是其中一个。 4、也有反馈的，大部分说是有些地点没有潮汐数据，这种情况大部分是因为没有那个观测点(因为我也无法创造观测点位，没那实力，都是推荐选着附近的地点，还有些是网络或定位问题，基本刷新或切换日期就能看到)，也有人反馈了真正的问题，虽然你留电话了，也没有贸然联系你，在这里感谢下这些用户： 137XXXX5197 、 186xxxx8191 、还有一些匿名的，谢谢你们提出的错误和意见。 ## 尴尬的地方 做到 v3 之后，我没有思路了。 陆陆续续迭代增加了不少功能，我自己也时常在分辨：哪些是大家真正需要的，哪些只是我主观觉得好用。 后台能看到访客来访，很多人打开、查询之后便离开了。我没法判断背后的原因：是数据不符合预期，还是没能快速找到想要的内容。当然我也明白，小程序本身就是轻量化工具，不少人本就是随用随走，这点我完全理解。 我有心把它做得更贴合大家的真实使用场景，只是暂时还摸不准真实的需求痛点。 所以想认真征集一轮，不光是好话，难听的也行。 ## 想听的具体问题 不用憋大的，随便答一条都有用： - 你打开它，第一眼最想看到什么？现在这块屏顺序对吗？ - 界面丑，具体丑在哪？配色、字体、图表、信息太挤，还是哪里都不对？ - 广告：底部 banner、开屏、或者干脆付费去广告，你能接受哪种？ - 你觉得最该砍掉的功能是哪个（这个我很想知道，砍比加难） - 还缺什么？我自己脑子里过过这些：大潮日历和提醒、赶海指数打分、摄影指数（火烧云/蓝调时刻/太阳方位）、海水温度、月相、打卡记录、海钓时段 - 如果你平时用别的同类工具，为什么留着它、没留我？这条最有价值 ## 关于回馈 被采纳的建议，以后会在这个版本里做出来。 到时候你带着当时在这帖里的回复（楼层号或自己的原话截图）来小程序里联系作者，我核对后，送一年 VIP。 VIP 现在就是去广告 + 后续的高级预报能力（比如三天火烧云、离线点位之类），具体按最终上线形态给，不会赖账，但功能还在做，先说清楚免得画大饼。 ## 最后 这帖有点长，谢谢看到这儿。 有用的继续骂，不用客气，说得难听但具体，我更喜欢听。如果不符合版规，跟我说一声我自己删。

projects.title: Show HN: Langfuse AI Gateway, open source rust gateway to trace every LLM call
projects.author: clemo_ra
projects.summary: Hi HN, this is Max, Marc and Clemens, co-founders of Langfuse, the open source tool for agent & observability & evals ( https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse ). It’s been a minute since our last Show HN in August 2023 ( https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=37310070 ) - we’ve been busy building out and serving our tracing & eval pieces over the past years and have been very lucky to build a successful company and open source project around it. Today, we are happy to show the beta of Langfuse AI Gateway: https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/tree/main/ai-gateway . You may ask, why an AI Gateway as our second product: it’s been one our community’s strongest asks + integration pattern that we’ve seen. We want to offer a scalable, reliable and secure way to solve for the gateway use case in the same way that we’ve done with tracing/evals over the past years. And we’ve recently grown our team with some excellent folks - expect to see more bigger bets from us. Our observability SDKs currently see the code you instrument. Much of a company's model traffic runs through code that is not or cannot be easily instrumented: coding agents like Pi, Claude Code and Codex, internal tools, scripts etc. Third party gateways are already popular ways to emit traces to Langfuse and we’re happy to now ship one natively. You change your base URL and your API key. Langfuse AI Gateway forwards the native request with a provider key that does not need to be distributed across the team. Right now, it doesn't translate between APIs, responses are relayed unchanged. This was a conscious decision to ensure stability for gateway users, as translation between e.g. OpenAI responses and Anthropic messages are imperfect and might lead to subtle failures in your agents. If you pass a traceparent header, the call lands inside your existing Langfuse traces. You can try by docker composing langfuse up and then on to http://localhost:3000 -- git clone https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse.git cd langfuse docker compose up -- On Cloud, each call becomes a Langfuse generation with tokens, cost, latency and time to first token. Prompts and outputs are recorded if you opt in. If you self-hosted you can also track nothing, not even metadata. Some details: - Written in Rust. Stateless, with no database; it talks only to the Langfuse platform and the providers. - 22MB Docker image. Under 3ms median overhead with tracing on, 1,000+ concurrent streams on 2 vCPUs. - MIT licensed. Self-host it with Docker Compose or Helm or use our Cloud version. - Your provider keys and contracts. We don't resell tokens. What’s next? - Budget caps per key, user, team - Custom model aliases and fallbacks - Guardrails - PII redaction - SCIM user provisioning We’ll be around & looking forward to all questions & comments

projects.title: Show HN: ReadyStack.dev – Bit-for-bit reproducible OSS containers
projects.author: readystack
projects.summary: https://readystack.dev If you are like me, coding LLMs made open source more important not less. A few months ago I wanted to see how far I could get using minimal LLM cost (local on two 3090s and one subscription) to automate OSS containers with a build recipe that matched bits. That project ended up as ReadyStack.dev. ReadyStack publishes free Community Edition containers for open-source applications. I designed it to be a low cost image standard that puts provenance as a first order concern. My goal was to see if I could build in trust with my images in a way nobody else had. Use the build recipe and match bits. Each release's build kit includes everything the build needs: upstream source pinned, the OS packages as .debs, the language dependencies, the base images saved by digest, fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. BUILD_OFFLINE.sh rebuilds with the network off, so mirrors dropping old packages don't matter, and VERIFY_OFFLINE.sh checks your digest against ours. We currently have 101 of 101 releases reproducing their published linux/amd64 digest in our clean-room rebuild process, which is just a trust signal, but an important one as we don't have much of, if at all. Certainly, not for free. For full disclosure, I built a sister project, ce.rodeo, which grades container images from all publishers, including ReadyStack.dev. Yes, it is a conflict of interest to grade my own images. I publish the measuring criteria and I needed a standard of what existed so I had to create a grading system first. Happy to hear suggestions. I started out to do something for OSS. I designed it to run on a skinny budget and it is doing that. It runs on donations, so far just mine. The bigger idea is that open-source software should be having its greatest era now that everyone has a DevOps genius at their fingertips. I chose to take a leap and build a platform to be part of that. Happy to answer questions.

projects.title: Show HN: Open-source firmware for 2011 Bowers and Wilkins Zeppelin Air
projects.author: fellowmartian
projects.summary: Just wanted to share something I've built. It's fully reverse engineered, running on an old 2.4 Linux kernel I found on Nokia HD-1, but with a modern all-Rust userspace. Support Airplay 2 and Snapcast. The Airplay 2 implementation synchronizes with real Apple devices down to 1ms in the multi-room configuration. Spotify support is present, but it doesn't work for me because of librespot key issues. It utilizes the MIPS co-processor cores I have found on it for audio decoding and crypto. There's no FPU on the ARM nor the MIPS, so all the codecs are reimplemented in fixed-point math and made to fit the very small shared SRAM buffers. The DSP board firmware is also completely replaced. It fixes all the complaints I had about the original device: no source auto-switching, USB audio would de-enumerate when the speaker went to sleep, volume keys were sending HID events instead of using the proper UAC status interrupt endpoint, etc. I tried getting 24b USB audio to work, but unfortunately the endpoint buffers on this old AVR32 are too small. The the network audio supports full 44.1/48/24b though. The Wi-Fi chip is very old, there's no upgrading that, so realtime ALAC on Airplay or PCM/FLAC on Snapcast can be spotty if the connection isn't perfect, but Ethernet works too. The iPod dock doesn't work, mainly because I can't find my old iPod anywhere to develop against. Send PRs if you have one! Also partly for vanity and partly for UX I updated the LED colors and FX.

projects.title: Show HN: Duck – Making DuckDB feel like Swift
projects.author: mihael
projects.summary: I was looking for a new database solution for my iOS and macOS apps. The original idea was pretty simple: bring the power O love about postgres onto the client side. I never liked CoreData. A long time ago I was using Realm because it solved my problem with slow batch insertions and brought reactivity. Nowadays there's SwiftData too, but I'm honestly not a fan of it at all. I'm in love with the server-side approach of working with SQL, like what I use with Vapor and what I originally built my SwifQL for. Then I found DuckDB, which kind of shares my love for postgres-style SQL and gives you a looooooot more power to play with on the client side. SuckDB already has an official Swift client, but it wasn't the application-level API I wanted to use in my apps. So I decided to build my own Swift layer around it. I'd already doing similar things with Bridges and SwifQL on the server side, so I brought a lot of those ideas with me. And here's what we have now: a beautiful, very Swiftly way of working with Duck and writing SQL: ``` import Duck struct Todo: Table { @Column("id") var id: UUID @Column("name") var name: String } let todos = try await Todo.all(on: .app) ``` There are more examples in the repo's readme, together with SwiftUI and UIKit example apps you can immediately play with. This is the first stable 1.0.0 release and it includes Codable integration, async/await, reactive queries, migrations, transactions, reusable prepared statements, connection pooling, bulk ingestion through DuckDB's Appender, native LIST/STRUCT values, and the SwiftStream/SQL DSL. Underneath it is the real, fresh DuckDB 2.0.0 engine. Right now Duck targets iOS15+ and macOS12+. I've also tested it on Linux. The engine itself supports many more platforms, but I haven't validated the Duck on those yet. I wanted a richer SQL engine with a beautiful Swift DSL, and I got it. I you also want to try something different on the client side, welcome to the Duck club. And since this is HN, here's a problem I haven't solved to my satisfaction yet. If you want to hear about any problems... I haven't found a silver bullet for the server-side migrations approach problem yet, so I kept migrations at the foundation level, and I'm going to experiment with one or more higher-level approaches on to of that. If you've dealt with the same problem, I'd genuinely love to hear how you approached it.

projects.title: Show HN: Cerulion – ROS 2-compatible robotics runtime with multi-process replay
projects.author: lakshays

github.name: cerulion-inc/cerulion
github.description: Cerulion (YC S24) gives AI agents a harness to control real robots. Our open-source runtime and harness give any AI agent a physical body, inside safety limits the robot enforces, and tools to autonomously debug recorded robot failures. It's ROS 2 compatible.

projects.summary: Hey HN! I'm Lakshay. Raveen and I have built Cerulion, a ROS2-compatible robotics runtime written in Rust. We've worked hard on lowering IPC transport latencies without making the single process tradeoff or forcing POD message types. These fast multi-process graphs can then be resimmed deterministically, and existing ROS2 nodes/launch files can run unmodified alongside native Cerulion Rust/Python code. Installation and quickstart (with a one-shot prompt for your favorite coding agent) here at the repo README: https://github.com/cerulion-inc/cerulion I worked on off-road autonomy during my PhD at MIT, and we kept running into inter-process latency in ROS (2 lidars and 6 cameras). Loaned messages need POD types, which nukes standard, vendor-agnostic Image/PointCloud2. We ended up running some hot paths in a brittle single process, which made debugging a nightmare. I'm sure you've seen the heisenbugs ROS-based stacks can produce, with no way to easily reproduce the consumption order or interleaving of callbacks. Valuable data of runtime failures on the robot was hard to use effectively without deterministic reproducibility. This is what we fix. Cerulion bags record per-input reads and scheduler traces alongside message content in standard MCAPs. cerulion bag play --resim all --verify re-executes node code on the recorded schedule and compares each byte for exact matches or within defined tolerances. Exit 0 is a match, 1 shows the first topic/frame that diverges, 6 shows schedule divergence and --report gives an optional CI verdict. Eligible ROS2 processes can replay deterministically as well. Here's the data loop: 1. Run: Dependency-ordered level-based DAG scheduler with periodic/data/sync triggers, I/O deadlines, backpressure, and automatic profiling for process partitioning. Each node by default free-runs in its own process while preserving deterministic replay. Live runs pause/resume, and UMWAIT/WFE parks idle consumers on CPUs that support it. Wall-clock reads and runtime thread spawns in user code rejected at compile time by macros. ROS 2 is supported with rmw_cerulion for Foxy, Humble, Jazzy and Lyrical, that lets you run ROS2 nodes/launch files unmodified in the same graph as native Cerulion nodes. LD_PRELOAD gives ROS2 code shared memory loans through std::vector/std::string. cerulion ros2 attach folds in already-running ROS2 robots, and cerulion ros2 run/launch lets you run existing ROS2 workspaces on Cerulion without any additional setup (with an optional automatic migrate suggested that rewrites C++ publish sites). 2. Move: iceoryx2 shared memory with no serialization, no payload copy and no payload-sized allocation, including for variable-length messages like sensor_msgs/Image and PointCloud2. Round trip latency for a 1MiB sensor_msgs/Image between two processes is 4.08µs p50, with a tight tail of 7.38µs p99 (under 2x p50), with recording on . This is default Cerulion, against 10.95 ms for default ROS 2 Jazzy. Cerulion's p50 and p99 stay flat from 64B to 16 MiB. 3. Capture: With this round-trip latency, there are no tradeoffs, not for process isolation and not for bagging. We can afford always-on or event-based logging. Flashback is our robot dashcam: keeps ~30s of all logs and message contents in memory and saves it automatically on process crashes, topic stalls or declared incidents/manual triggers. 4. Reach: A free account lets you pair robots and desks, letting all your devices find each other with no config, IP addresses or discovery chatter. Pubsub is authenticated and on-demand, with signed grants that the robot verifies offline. We use Iroh to hole-punch or relay over WAN, and mDNS over LAN to transmit data using QUIC. Remote topics mirror into local shared memory, and each device has a single network gateway. 5. Diagnose: cerulion doctor scans for compile/run-time issues (better than Windows Troubleshooter I promise) and suggests fixes. Hindsight is an early access MCP to let agents analyze your bags. To get started: go to the repo, install Cerulion with the curl one-liner, and paste the prompt in Claude Code/Codex: https://github.com/cerulion-inc/cerulion#quickstart-run-reco... . Or shift your own gears, it's all in the repo that you should star! The CLI needs a free account, which we use to make device pairing as easy as AirDrop USED to be ;) Everything runs on Linux (x86_64/ARM64), macOS and Android (JNI), with more platforms coming. We'd love to hear your feedback! If you run ROS 2 on a real robot, point this at your stack and tell us what breaks. Docs: https://docs.cerulion.com Site: https://cerulion.com

projects.title: Show HN: Stop the app permission popups on macOS
projects.author: icyfox
projects.summary: Hey HN, I maintain a few Mac apps as side projects. Most of them involve permissions of some kind (microphone, screen recording) and I've always been annoyed by the abrupt permission granting popup that Mac will pop up whenever you request access: "MyApp would like to access your microphone" Don't allow | Allow "Allow MyApp to access devices on the local network" Don't allow | Allow etc etc I'm empathetic to Apple wanting to shock people out of their complacency - but the experience feels below the standard that people expect from their native apps. It feels almost adversarial. The Codex Computer Use onboarding was far better. It pops up a hovering window below the System Settings screen that you drag into the list. At this point you'll just be asked to confirm your password/TouchID, since the OS knows you're trying to add the specific app to a specific permission category. It does the same thing if you manually + add an app from your disk. I hadn't seen this paradigm anywhere else, but it seemed like the obvious way to improve the experience while still staying within the operating system constraints. I reproduced the underlying logic in Swift and bundled it into a library to check for your current permissions & display a managed window to request whichever ones your app needs. You're also welcome to import the authorization buttons explicitly so you can style them to your app's need. The Github GIF will do a better job of explaining the full UX. If you end up using it drop me a line.

projects.title: Show HN: Apron Chat Protocol
projects.author: shazow
projects.summary: Hi HN friends - I've been obsessed with chat protocols for ages - one previous project is ssh-chat ( https://ssh.chat/ ) I come bringing a new kind of chat protocol that I've been working on since I spent quite a lot of time exploring the 14 other competing standards we've come up with in the past few decades. The protocol details are here: https://apron.chat I'm hoping that Apron will better reflect our needs beyond 2026, which I expect will move more and more toward semi-private chats rather than global social networks. Come say hi on the live public demo: https://web.apron.chat Some fun facts: - The demo server runs in a Cloudflare Durable Worker. It's quite efficient, since it's hibernated except for when a message comes in. Easy to self-host this in the free tier. - Despite the JSON protocol being intentionally unabbreviated ("message" instead of "msg", etc), a typical Apron session still uses almost half as much bandwidth and messages compared to an equivalent Matrix or XMTP session. This is largely because Apron minimizes the number of roundtrips and state required for common chat scenarios. Also it compresses very nicely! - The official reference client is a PWA (Apron Web), we also have a TUI, macOS, and an iOS implementation by third party Apron-enjoyers. There's two reference server implementations (Cloudflare worker in TS and a Go implementation), plus a bunch of minimal implementations. - My favourite fun capability is embedding streaming messages, great for LLM outputs. This can be done just by piping to a curl command, no additional dependencies. There's also a mode for streaming a terminal (by piping something like `script` from util-linux which handles row/col/baud flushing, no special dependencies either). See section 4.8 for details: https://apron.chat/protocol#48-embeds-and-avatars

projects.title: Show HN: DeployAngel – A verdict in ~20 minutes if a deploy broke production
projects.author: jkowens
projects.summary: Hey there, I'm looking for feedback on a release verification tool I'm building. https://www.deployangel.com I decided to build this after an issue popped up with a recent Rails upgrade. We upgraded a Rails app to 8.1 and picked up a new default that changes the order after_commit callbacks run. Our upload code started telling the virus scanner about files before they were saved to S3, and the scanner just quietly dropped them. No exceptions were raised and uploads sat in "processing" for days. We should have had alarms in place, we know that now but I wondered if there could be some type monitoring that would just have noticed the change. I did some checking and the callback route went from roughly 27 requests an hour to zero when we deployed. That seems like a fairly easy change in behavior to automatically raise an alarm. So after a few weekends working with Claude I have a new tool. A small agent sends one aggregated payload per minute. Then the server compares each release with the last one it cleared. It looks at things like error rates, latency per route, traffic that collapses, and missing job runs. The server then returns a verdict if the release cleared or not. Currently I have agents for Rails, Django, FastAPI, and ASP.NET Core. It will work best for teams that deploy often and the app gets steady traffic. It's not meant to replace error monitoring tools like Sentry, but to work alongside them. Here's a recent release of its own: https://app.deployangel.com/share/KAaurrfRHcw43ZrjkWst2DLY?r... The agents are MIT-licensed. It's completely free right now, with a free tier planned. https://github.com/DeployAngel I'm looking for a few teams to run it on a real app for a couple of weeks. I'd love to hear if it surfaces issues that other monitoring and alarms miss. Of course I'm hoping it proves to be useful, but if not, that's good information too.

projects.title: Show HN: MergeMax, a monthly ranking of public merged PRs on GitHub
projects.author: diancodes
projects.summary: Hi HN, the main idea around MergeMax is that the user can look themselves up and compare themselves against all the other people on the board. No sign-in required. We currently support monthly and daily leaderboards. I built MergeMax since I kept seeing people post on X about @poteto's merge count and I knew I could probably create something to easily see her and other popular dev's GitHub public PRs. I quickly found out however that her PRs aren't visible via our methods, since most of her PRs are private/not on GitHub. I also wanted to create a place where people can easily see the amount of merges top accounts do each month, now that agents have the ability to create thousands of PRs themselves. Currently we only support public PRs as well as the contribution total that gets provided by GitHub directly: - A public PR only counts if it's public, merged, and authored by the account that's being looked up, and merged within the specified period. - I use GitHub's search API for PR counts. In a single GraphQL query we ask for 1 day per alias (is:pr is:merged is:public author:X merged:DATE), a whole month costs about 1 rate-limit point. If we had to page through PRs it would cost about 400 points per busy account. - Initially I tried GH Archive first, but PR events there no longer say whether a PR was merged. Current limitations include: - People that merged their own PRs also count. - Agent workflows can increase a person's PR count by a lot. So a bot can generate thousands of small PRs. - Private work and pushes directly to main don't show as public PRs. Those profiles do, however, show up in GitHub's contribution count if they've activated private contributions on GitHub. I had to seed about 1,000 accounts at launch and anyone who's been looked up since is also tracked. We obviously cannot track every single account on GitHub. It really became one of my most fun projects to work on. Especially loved creating the colorscheme/theme. Itterating through top 3 leaderboard designs, user profile look & feel, etc. I do support sponsor cards like some other popular similar sites but we don't have any sponsors yet. The stack I used was Tanstack Start deployed to Vercel with Convex as the backend. I'm open to any questions and feedback regarding the site, how it functions etc. Also would love to hear what you would like to see added to profiles, new boards, etc?

projects.title: Show HN: Collection of Beauty–a walkable 3D museum of public-domain art
projects.author: trebeljahr
projects.summary: Hi HN, this is Collection of Beauty, a walkable, multi-floor 3D museum, based on a collection of art that I handpicked with 4000+ works. History: I've spent some time earlier this year just browsing Wikipedia public domain art for literally hours on end, downloading everything that I liked or appreciated, just asking myself do I find this beautiful on some level? The result is this... Well, not quite ^^ In the end I had a large folder with a bunch of images in it that begged the question: can I make this more useful somehow? Like, it's nice to have all these images sitting on my hard disk somehow but I want to share this with other people as a Collection of Beauty. But they were just images, nothing else. A bit of wrangling with AI later and now this website exists. It has a 3D museum you can walk through, with multiple floors. The images are displayed at their real sizes relative to one another and the room layouts etc. And yes, the Mona Lisa is that small ^^ Luckily Wikimedia file names can be reverse searched and therefore I had access to the entire Wikimedia metadata against each of the images to sort them and create a metadata catalogue that allows for different ways of slicing through the images, like showing things like: "similar artists", "other artists the artist knew personally", or just "epoch/style" related ideas. I also sorted paintings by color on one of the sub pages, because I thought that would be nifty. If you find something that is clearly in the wrong epoch or by the wrong artist or the wrong size, has a wrong title or whatever, please file an issue on GitHub ( https://github.com/trebeljahr/collection-of-beauty ). Also I know of this other project that did something similar (though they mapped literally all art that ever existed), but I swear I had this idea on my own, sometimes different people come up with the same stuff. https://artmuseum.artfrompixels.com/ When a friend sent this to me, I took some inspiration though and made the frames and lighting and general 3D experience much more beautiful as well. I also had to facepalm myself and whisper: "why didn't I think of this myself," and then added some (public domain or freely licensed) music playing in the background as you look at the paintings. The whole thing is deployed with Cloudflare workers because it's 90% static and Cloudflare has very very generous free tiers. Also credit where credit is due, the set of flowers from Redoute is from https://www.c82.net/redoute/ one of my favorite websites of all time ^^ Under the hood the image rendering in the 3D walkthrough does something cool with LOD texture variants where rooms determine when to load each painting's resolution based on a bunch of heuristics, keeping the experience relatively lightweight and fast (hopefully). It should load the really big scans only if you jam up your nose right into a painting. If some beautiful but more modern art is missing (MC Escher?!) then this is because of copyright issues. There are quite a few artists whose work I would love to include in here but where there is still copyright on the images and therefore I can't afaik. Also, if you have more Public Domain art, that you personally really like, please share that with me too, would love to include more stuff in here (if I like it ofc ^^). Link to Wikipedia, name of the artist to check out, name of the painting, etc.

projects.title: Show HN: Lettercamp – open-source static blog framework
projects.author: justswim
projects.summary: Hi HN, I’m Eric and I’m building Lettercamp, an open-source static blog framework. The repo is at https://github.com/lettercamp/lettercamp and the homepage is online at https://www.lettercamp.com . Writing good content has always been the #1 way that I’ve grown the reach of products I’ve worked on in the past. However, it’s always bothered me how many little things get in the way of writing and publishing high quality, first party content onto the web. Building a performant, SEO-optimized blog from scratch was always distracting from development on the actual product, and setting up a 3rd party CMS meant that my content always lived in someone else’s database. Storing content in a non-markdown format also made it difficult to draft and edit with the help of an AI agent. Lettercamp is a modern approach to creating a content site. It ships with all the little features you’d expect in a blog: pagination, authors, metadata, search, cross linking, related posts and more. It’s also statically built, which means that all your content lives in markdown in your codebase, so a deployed version is performant with no database to maintain. This means that you can focus on writing good content instead of vibe-coding a whole blog. I want to add more features to the framework over time, including better support for AI agents, built in localization, email sign ups, and more. The repo is released under the MIT license so that anyone can use the framework to create a content site. The goal isn’t to charge individual developers. The monetization path is to provide a cloud hosted version, that has an online editor that content teams can use. The main advantage of this is to decouple the blog from product deploys, so that teams can publish content without needing to push code. I would love to get your feedback on if this is a problem that might resonate with you or your team. I know that a lot of products create a /blog section at some point, and I wonder what solutions people are using today. My hope is that over time, Lettercamp can be the go-to solution for teams looking to set this up. Try it out: https://github.com/lettercamp/lettercamp and let me know what you think!

projects.title: Show HN: Rebuilding Amazon SES in Rust
projects.author: auscaster
projects.summary: I'm Kam, co-founder and CTO of Nitrosend. Email is our lifeblood, so we've been gradually moving our email sending onto bare-metal servers and IPs we control. We wanted to make that move without rewriting the application code already calling Amazon SES. So we built NitroMTA, an open-source SES replacement in Rust. We kept our existing SES v2 sending calls and changed the endpoint and credentials to send through our own engine. We've been running it in production for a few weeks, moving more mail over as we warm our IPs and build reputation with each mailbox provider. Keep the SES integration For an application using boto3, this is the client configuration: import boto3 ses = boto3.client( "sesv2", region_name="us-east-1", endpoint_url="https://mail.example.com", ) For the SES v2 sending operations we support, the existing calls keep working. We test the official JavaScript, Python and Ruby SDKs against the engine, along with Nodemailer and django-ses. The compatibility page lists the operations and differences from SES: https://nitromta.com/docs/compatibility/ Measuring against KumoMTA and Postfix In our published 2 November comparison, NitroMTA sustained 3.16 times KumoMTA's throughput and 4.11 times Postfix's. These numbers measure SMTP submission and delivery. Engine Messages per second NitroMTA 3,313 KumoMTA 1,048 Postfix with OpenDKIM 806 Each engine had four CPU cores and 2 GiB of memory on the same AWS c7gd.metal bare-metal server, with its queue on local NVMe. The workload used 16 KiB messages, authenticated SMTP submission, TLS on submission and delivery, and RSA-2048 DKIM signing. Every engine committed a message to disk before acknowledging it. The figures are medians of three interleaved runs per engine. The quick profile searches for the highest rate meeting its latency budgets using ten-second load steps, delivering to one receiver site with no added network delay. Across the nine runs, the harness sent 1.35 million messages and checked that each arrived once, with its body intact and its DKIM signature valid. KumoMTA used its RocksDB spool with set_force_sync(true) to meet the same acceptance contract. KumoMTA documents that this forces database-wide flushes and can substantially reduce performance. The comparison is for that synchronous-acceptance contract; the harness also supports measuring its default asynchronous mode separately. The method, configurations, exact versions and raw results are published, and you can run the comparison with cargo harness quick: https://nitromta.com/docs/benchmarks/ Give each IP a budget for each provider An IP needs a sending history with the receivers it sends to. We need to decide how much volume it gets today, what earns it more tomorrow, and what makes us back off. We track the budget by sending IP and receiver group. That lets us hold an IP's Gmail cap while increasing its cap elsewhere, or lower its Outlook.com cap when Microsoft's responses call for it. With warmup enabled, the shipped ladder starts at 50 messages a day. A day needs enough SMTP outcomes to test its cap before it earns an increase. Complaints, failures, deferrals and throttling can hold the cap or move it down a rung. The Outlook.com defaults take fourteen clean daily increases to reach 10,000 messages a day. The default ladder takes seven. Both are configurable. Before any of this, the host needs outbound port 25 and reverse DNS control for its sending addresses. The domains need SPF, DKIM and DMARC, and bounce and complaint reports need somewhere to arrive. We put the setup checks in nitromta doctor, which prints the missing records. Provider feedback and durability details continue in a reply.

projects.title: Show HN: App to help parents find, plan, and review outings with their kids
projects.author: brendanperry
projects.summary: Background: My wife and I have 4 boys 4 and under, so we have to get them out of the house consistently to stay sane. Finding good places to take them can be a frustrating process that involves digging through Facebook groups and Google/Yelp reviews that aren't always relevant for parents. The idea: An app that has reviews of places to take your kids by parents. No AI generated magic, just real people documenting their experience. Sproutings has a map of places parents have been with some ideas for new places to try. You can also coordinate outings with other parents using an outing planning tool. The challenge: I sat on this idea for a long time because of the challenge that is mapping data. The best POI source you can think of is Google, but their terms are unfriendly and prices don't work for an indie dev. Other better priced options still do not let you store the POI data from their API in your own database. I was determined to have my own map view of all of the places people have reviewed, so I needed coordinates. The tech: My solution to this was a postgres database full of data I imported and filtered from OSM. This gives me full control over the data to with what I want. So now I have a really cool map view with pins that can scale to millions with no problem using pmtiles. The client side is built with React Native. This was just so I could easily launch on web and mobile. On web, RN has a hard time with SEO, so I had to display some raw HTML / CSS here and there. There are also plenty of challenges with bugs that would only appear on certain platforms, so keeping everything aligned was a constant game of whack-a-mole. Conclusion: I have a picture in my mind of a Sproutings map overflowing with places reviewed by parents, but the reality is that we have a chicken and egg problem. A platform that relies on user engagement to provide value isn't valuable until people have engaged. However, I'm hoping that I can reach more and more parents that would find it valuable and continue to expand its reach. I'd love to hear of any and all feedback! Thanks for reading.

projects.summary: I'm new here, and little nervous about posting, but here goes. I'm not a newbie. I started programming in BASIC when my dad bought home a TRS-80 Model I in 1980, when I was 16. Other than a 9-year stint as active duty military, I've spent 46 years either personally or professionally working in tech. I've programmed in RPG using punch cards for an IBM /System360, and COBOL on a DEC pdp 11/34. I've worked professionally with VB, C#, SQL Server, ColdFusion, PHP, and more. I've seen a lot of technologies come and go. So this ain't the first time I've jogged around this track. Here's the problem I wanted to solve: I hate WordPress. I mean, as a concept, it's fine, but I used to have a fairly popular motorcycle blog on WP that got trashed by hackers. I've also run into that problem with customers. When hackers find a wordpress site, they just bang on it like a drum. It's a pain. It's also a pain just to manage it, with a wild-west plugin system where plugins constantly fall in and out of compatibility. I'm also not a huge fan of PHP, but since it comes stock with pretty much every shared hosting service, where a lot of my web work is done, it's kind of the default for doing web stuff. Back in about 2006 or so, I built my own blogging software, which I called .Blog, as an ASP.NET deal in C#. It took me about 6 months to build, start to finish. I didn't have time to keep up with it, which is why I defaulted back to WP sometime around 2014. I migrated to Grav when I ran across it (I guess around 2020 or so), and I liked that. But Grav ran into some issues, and development on it really slowed. In the past year or so, the company I work for has been delving into using Claude Code, and I got an idea. What if I could just use Claude Code to build a CMS that has everything I want, and nothing I don't? This project is the result of that idea. I designed the specifications for what I wanted it to do, and let Claude Code handle the actual code writing. I started with a flat-file, markdown-based flat-file CMS, and iterated on that. Fiddling around with markdown files and folders started to get tedious, so I moved towards SQLite as the back-end, to create a system as self-contained and easy to use as possible. This project is, I think, the final result of that idea. This project, from start to finish, took about 2 weeks to build using Laravel/Filament/PHP with Claude Code, compared to the 6 months it took to build .Blog by hand, 20 years ago. Cripes, I'm old. Personally, I'm pretty pleased with how this project turned out. I'm running two public websites on it. I'd be interested to hear what others think.
