projects.title: Show HN: EarthData – find places to visit or live that match what you care about
projects.author: 11thEarlOfMar
projects.summary: Hi HN, A few years ago, I was trying to find the place on Earth that had the optimal combination of attributes to vacation to or live. I couldn't find anything that wasn't a marketing funnel or was limited in geography. So I built EarthData essentially for myself, but others might find it useful. There are two modes: "visit" for a trip (travel month, length of stay, things to do) and "live" for relocation or retirement (housing, healthcare, day-to-day fit). The way it operates is to allow the user to sculpt the attributes they care about in where they visit on vacation or live. Rate and rank what matters to you. And it will returns 10 initial places, down to specific towns, with a written explanation of why each one fits. From there, the user can expand on places that look interesting, and ultimately pull a TRIP KIT with full itinerary, web links to venues, packing list and other information. A few design choices: - It's anonymous. No account, no email required, and preferences live in your browser's local storage. Nothing is tied to a named profile, your preferences are sent to xAI's API to generate matches, but without any PII. - No ads and no advertising cookies. - I went with a mid-century travel graphic design. To me, it evokes nostalgia and romance for international travel. - It supports 10 different languages. - The initial top 10 Matching is free. The only paid part is an optional $3.75 trip kit for a single place (itinerary, 10 matched activities, checklist, PDF). It covers the Google Places API costs for venues and links, which seem oddly 'expensive'. - Matching uses an LLM (currently xAI's Grok) to generate and reason about candidates, which get shaped into place cards, maps, short videos and activities. One area I struggled with was how to group and refine the attribute selections. Higher slider levels reveal finer-grained choices and give that topic more weight. So if it matters a lot, you can really dial in what you're looking for. If it doesn't matter to you, you can skip entirely. If you see any that seem out of line, please point it out. It was a lot of work to make sense with the slider settings, and I'm not convinced it's dialed in. Finally, if you're looking for something that doesn't have a selection, you can free-form a must-have before submitting. Feedback welcome!

As you can imagine, this was inconvenient and became time consuming. I tried keeping the games in my own calendar for the season, typing them in myself. But the entries kept needing to change: broadcasters reschedule games, cup draws add new fixtures partway through the season, the Playoff in the American major leagues starts, etc. Every time that happened, I had to go back and fix it by hand. So I built Matchday. It streamlines all of that, keeping you up to date with all of your teams' games right from your own calendar. Not another app, just a calendar I already look at every day, and the games stay up to date on their own. I tried to make a straightforward UX (and probably failed): You pick your teams, set an optional name for the calendar feed, select the Calendar type, then subscribe in it. In case of European clubs, you can mark them as "follow everywhere" and you get all their different cup games as well. Currently it supports men's and women's football, NHL, NBA, WNBA, and NFL. If somebody is interested, following a national football team is completely free, no email is needed. Otherwise, at least an email is required. I started building it for the World Cup, and was quite popular amongst my friends and colleagues but it is still a super small side project and I would appreciate any feedback, especially on the UX side.

projects.title: 一天上线了一个 Roblox 新游戏的资料站
projects.author: yuchuan520
projects.summary: 最近 Roblox 上有个 JoJo 题材的新游戏 Stand Out 很火，同时在线 5 万多人，官方 Discord 17 万多成员。这类 Roblox 游戏的官方资料一般放在 Trello 上，但 Trello 的内容在 Google 里几乎搜不到（搜索结果只显示 "No information is available for this page"），手机上翻 1000 多张卡片也很痛苦。 所以做了一个非官方的资料站：https://standout-trello.com 目前有这些内容： - 兑换码：按官方 Trello 里 Active / Expired 两个分组来区分，附兑换步骤和"码用不了"排查表 - 全部 Stand：45 个已上线的 Stand，可按稀有度筛选，写了每个怎么获得 - 箭的种类：6 种道具的合成配方、排除的稀有度、官方公布的概率 - 更新日志、Wiki 索引、Discord 真假辨别 几个做的时候的体会： 1. 数据准确比内容多重要。上线当天官方就换了一块新 Trello 板，旧板停更；同一天还有 3 个兑换码过期。好几个竞品站还把过期码列成可用。所以每个页面底部都列了数据来自哪几张 Trello 卡片、什么时候核对的，读者可以自己点过去验证。 2. Trello 公开板可以直接读 JSON（/1/boards/{id}/cards），写了个同步脚本，只更新事实字段，人工补充的内容保留不覆盖。 3. 技术栈：Next.js 静态导出 + Cloudflare Pages，代码放 GitLab。整站静态，移动端 Lighthouse 基本都在 97–100。下一步准备用 Cloudflare 定时触发重新构建，构建时自动拉 Trello 数据，这样兑换码过期能几小时内同步。 站是非官方的，和开发团队没有关系。欢迎提意见，也欢迎做游戏站的朋友交流。

projects.summary: 一个纯本地音乐播放器（iPhone / iPad / Apple 芯片 Mac），无账号、无广告、不上传音频。1.7.3 共 19 处改动，补的是几件一直欠着的事：能播的格式少一块、桌面上没得用、从服务器拿歌得先存到「文件」。 格式：MP3 / M4A / MP4 / AAC / FLAC / ALAC / WAV / AIFF·AIF / CAF / MP1·MP2 / OGG·OGA / Opus / DSF·DFF / APE；APE 与 FLAC 内嵌 CUE 也认，旁边放 .lrc 就是逐行歌词。另有 10 段参数均衡器与 ReplayGain。 ![](https://i.imgur.com/bkiQd0O.png) ## 1.7.3 更新 1. APE 现在能直接播（Pro）。不是导入时先转一道 WAV，是边读边解码：后台线程按块取 PCM 进环形缓冲，均衡器和播放器照常取数据，全程没有中间文件。为什么不做缓存转码——APE 无损，一首五分钟解成 WAV 就是 50–100MB，一张专辑几百兆，首次播放还得等转完；实测解码速度是实时的 20–100 倍，余量足够，没必要拿磁盘换时间。代价是只做立体声：多声道的 APE（DVD-A 抓的那种）直接拒绝播放，不静默下混。 2. 整轨 + .cue 的专辑按曲目分开。APE 与 FLAC 内嵌的 CUE 也认，不用在文件旁边再放一份。 3. Mac 上原生运行。不另做一套 Mac 界面，同一份工程跑在 Apple 芯片的 Mac 上，曲库、播放器、Wi-Fi 传歌、导入全是 iPad 那一套；长页面可以按住鼠标拖动滚动，和系统里其它应用一致。取舍：需要 Apple 芯片的 Mac，Intel 机器不在范围内。 4. WebDAV 导入。浏览服务器目录，挑文件或整个文件夹，落到本地和「文件」导入走同一条管线——命名、去重、元数据、CUE 展开都一致，不会出现「服务器来的歌和本地的不一样」。服务器密码进钥匙串，不写明文配置。取舍：单向的「挑一次、落到本地」，不做双向同步，也不扫你服务器上的整个曲库。 5. 睡眠定时独立成页（Pro）：圆环选时长，1 分钟到 14 小时，结束前淡出；倒计时可以暂停，想多听两首按一下，不用重设。 6. iPad / Mac 键盘快捷键：空格播放暂停，⌘← ⌘→ 切歌，⇧⌘← ⇧⌘→ 快进快退，⌘R 切循环、⌘S 切随机；设置里新增一页列全。 7. 其余几处：音频或整个文件夹拖到文件夹页即导入；长按一首歌直接改标题、歌手、专辑、封面；歌单、收藏和自定义标题导出成带版本号的文件，换设备导回去；「存储」页拆开显示音频、封面、歌词、数据和缓存各占多少；关联文件夹保留目录结构，新文件不用手动重扫；文件在 App 外被改名或移动后，歌单按路径 → 文件名 → 标题与歌手三步找回；搜索更快，大小写和变音符号都不敏感；歌单页加了「最近播放」。 8. 修了几处老毛病。最要紧的是换 Apple 账号后 Pro 不再消失：只有商店明确告知「已撤销」才锁回免费，账号切换、离线、商店没回应都保留上一次判定——宁可晚锁一个退款的，也不误锁一个付过钱的。另外修了：中日韩标签的曲名不再变问号；同时带新旧标题标签的歌显示正确标题；横屏在歌词处下滑能收起播放器；系统关掉实时活动时，锁屏歌词页会说明原因并给出开关入口。 免费下载；Pro 一次性买断，不订阅。DSD 与 APE 播放、保存自己的 EQ 调音、播放倍速、睡眠定时、全部主题与播放器样式、备用图标与自定义封面、三行锁屏歌词在 Pro 里，其余都能免费用。 ## 送 10 个码 ``` 8EKFE6TETNPAFN6TKH TPH66L6FMHRTM773XF 4L4W4XL3F7XWTTWETA MAPF4Y3TR3FP4K7FPL 86ET78FWRRXARMNXKP MKYRXKJMHWLTKX7JPF HHRHENAW7834HTRR7M AMEHKARATPTWXA8XNJ WMPER7TRL7XN6AKPT8 L37NTNEFJFK7EWEPR7 ``` 有问题大家可以进群反馈 ![](https://i.imgur.com/vcwUVqA.png)

projects.title: Show HN: Hello Triangle, a puzzle game where you build a GPU
projects.author: icedlatte
projects.summary: I've been working on a game Hello Triangle for a while. In the game, you build a GPU one part at a time by wiring circuits, and renders a picture on the screen with what your circuit computes. I have a free demo available that goes up to drawing a triangle, while I'm still working on the rest of the game. You don't start from logic gates. The game starts with adders and comparators. Every wire just carries a fixed point number, and there are no bit widths to think about. The reason of using fixed point numbers is that veteran players of Turing Complete can skip the bits part they already player, while players who are new to programming can still jump right in. The circuit simulator is written in Go and the game UI is written in Godot, and they communitate through stdio. I also built a score server that players can upload their scores and compare with each other through score histograms. The demo is available on Steam (Windows/macOS/Linux), there's also an itch.io build if you don't use Steam. Curious what you think, and where you get stuck!

Upload a WAV/MP3 or paste a Suno link: it maps tempo, sections and lyrics, plans a storyboard you can edit, then renders scenes that cut on the beat. Free storyboard + chorus preview. No real people, no face swaps.

projects.summary: Sidefoot is the clubhouse for your pickup soccer career. Paste the score from your group chat and the Match Official logs it. Your crew gets a league table ranked by points per game, you get a career card, and you can find a crew that plays every week.

projects.title: Show HN: Four bite-sized chess puzzle games built on micro-boards
projects.author: navalsaini
projects.summary: Most chess apps try to replicate the classic 64-square experience. Over the last few years, I’ve been doing the opposite—breaking chess down into fast, bite-sized mobile games on smaller boards, each designed to isolate and gamify a single skill: Firstchess: Bite-sized lessons to learn the fundamentals on a compact board. Halfchess: Focused purely on endgame thinking on a smaller grid. Phantom Chess: Blind/memory-based chess on a mini board. Schmess: Real-time speed chess where multiple pieces move simultaneously. You can try all four live apps at https://halfchess.com . I plan to build more chess/poker mini games if I can figure out a distribution for these. If you know any media outlets or micro influencers who can cover my games, do let me know.

projects.title: Cozy Garden
projects.summary: Grow your own little pixel-art garden. Plant seeds, watch crops grow in real time, and harvest them to earn coins and XP. Unlock achievements, explore different crops, and build a garden that's uniquely yours. Features: - Plant and grow multiple types of crops - Watch crops progress through growth stages - Harvest for coins and experience points - Buy seeds from the in-game shop - Unlock achievements and track your progress - Explore player profiles and leaderboards

projects.title: SmartPoster

projects.title: Launchproof

Connect Claude and it works inside your coaching account: 134 tools that create clients, build programs from your exercise library, draft broadcasts, and set up lead funnels. Your clients get a real app: workouts as a full-screen vertical video deck, an AI assistant inside, you in the chat. Free for 3 clients, then a flat $49/month. No per-client fees.

projects.title: MyBodyiQ
projects.summary: Track meals, calories, macros, hydration, exercise, weight, medications, appointments, and health goals with MyBodyiQ.

projects.title: KesPrep
projects.summary: KesPrep looks across your public Chess.com or Lichess games to find recurring mistakes, then points you to positions from your own games to study. Stockfish evaluates the moves; KesPrep turns the results into a training focus. It is free during early access, and you can try it without creating an account.

projects.title: RPG Haven
projects.summary: RPG Haven makes finding your next tabletop RPG group easier. Browse games, meet fellow players, and apply to join campaigns near you or online. Whether you play D&D, Pathfinder, Call of Cthulhu, or something more obscure, find your next adventure or the players for your own game.

projects.title: Niche Dance Move AI Video Generator
projects.summary: Animate one photo with Low-key Groove, Heel-toe Bounce or Arm Frames. Preview each dance and compare its source photo, then choose Basic or Pro, resolution and optional music. Check the live credit quote before generating, review the result and download your AI dance video. Built with Viral Video AI; motion and likeness can vary.

projects.title: Fellmark
projects.summary: Fellmark is a fantasy steampunk survival game on smooth voxel ground about two kilometres deep, and all of it can be dug. Mine ore veins, smelt and forge thirteen metals from copper to voidstone, build from the foundations up, survive the cold and the dark, sail the fjords, and in the endgame build automated factories. It's in closed testing on Windows, with online co-op and offline single-player. There's a free demo on itch.io with no time limit.

projects.title: Recipians: Daily Recipe App
projects.summary: Discover your next favorite meal with Recipians — 40,000+ recipes, personalized daily suggestions, step-by-step cooking, nutrition info, and an optional personal health log. Whether you know what to cook or need inspiration, Recipians finds meals that match your tastes, ingredients, dietary preferences, and the moment. Explore 40,000+ recipes across cuisines, ingredients, meal types, and diets — Indian, Thai, Italian, Mexican, breakfasts, dinners, snacks, desserts, vegetarian dishes, and more.

projects.title: MaxBot
projects.summary: MaxBot pushes your Twitch subs, VIPs and mods into Discord roles the moment they change, and takes the role off when a sub lapses. It also runs a watch-time economy with 15 games that work in Twitch chat and Discord, automod, custom commands, timed messages and stream overlays you lay out in a visual editor. It's hosted, so it keeps running when your PC is off, and one account runs every channel you're part of. Free to start; paid tiers from $5 a month.

projects.title: 球X (QIUX.AI)
projects.summary: 球X（QIUX.AI）是一款面向全球足球爱好者的 AI 体育智能与球迷社交平台，致力于将实时比分、专业赛事数据、AI 智能分析和全球球迷社区融为一体。 在球X，用户可以实时追踪全球足球赛事、查看比赛比分与球队数据，使用自主打造的垂直体育 AI 助手获取赛前分析、赛事研判和数据洞察。每场比赛都拥有专属讨论空间，让球迷分享观点、交流战术、参与赛事预测，并在赛后共同复盘。 我们希望改变传统体育平台单向获取信息的体验，让每一场比赛不仅值得观看，更值得分析、讨论和参与。 QIUX.AI 不只是一个比分网站，而是 AI 体育智能与足球社交社区的结合。 无论你是资深足球迷、赛事数据爱好者，还是喜欢与全球球迷交流的体育用户，都欢迎加入球X。 探索球X，开启全新的足球体验 🌐 https://qiux.ai

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Senrelay（续境）：本地优先的 macOS 多 Agent 会话接力与 15 宿主配置工作台
projects.author: qingsongcui

github.name: qingsongcui/ContextCore
github.description: Senrelay · 续境 — Local-first macOS multi-Agent conversation relay, source-linked persistent memory, and unified host configuration workbench.

projects.summary: GitHub 开源协议：MIT（完全免费、无需登录账号、零遥测） 平时高强度用 Claude Code、Codex CLI、Cursor 和 OpenCode 写代码，经常被两件琐事卡住： 1. 额度见底或切换工具时上下文断层：在 Claude Code 里排查完一半的问题，切到 Codex 或 Cursor 又得重新解释背景，很多贴进剪贴板的“自动摘要”还会把关键错误日志或边界条件丢掉； 2. 多宿主配置越改越乱：不同工具的 MCP JSON、TOML 和规则文件路径各不相同，手动修改很容易写坏原有字段或互相覆盖。 所以做了 Senrelay · 续境（ContextCore） —— 一个本地优先（local-first）的 macOS 原生多 Agent 工作台： 单指令跨工具原文接力（/contextcore）：在任意新工具里输入 /contextcore（或直接说“接着做”），先返回简短不掉帧的会话候选表（保留 Git Worktree 分支消歧）；选定后由接手 Agent 通过 readconversationmessages 按预算分页读取原始对话在本地压缩续写，支持“仅复盘待命（mustnotexecute=true）”与 discussiononly 防误改护栏。 双层工作记忆与原文溯源：区分当前任务状态（workingtasks）与长期规范/经验（contents），所有记忆绑定原话引用并支持冲突检测与版本回滚。 15 个编码宿主的事务化配置管理：内置 6 个核心上下文宿主 + 9 个扩展宿主的原生路径解析与结构化写入（支持 JSON / JSONC / JSON5 / TOML / YAML），写入前自动落盘备份快照；本地 FTS5 全文检索（默认不下载外部模型，完全运行在 127.0.0.1）。 安装与适用边界说明 当前 Public Beta（v1.0.0-beta.2）仅支持 Apple Silicon（arm64）macOS 14.0+（Windows/Linux 暂不支持）；安装包采用本地 ad-hoc 签名，首次打开前清一次下载隔离属性即可： bash brew install --cask qingsongcui/tap/senrelay xattr -cr /Applications/Senrelay.app 在线速查文档：15 个 AI 编程宿主配置路径与安全写入规则 实战工作流说明：跨 Agent 会话接力与额度交接指南

projects.title: Balak City
projects.summary: Balak City is a free open-world city game you play right in the browser or inside Telegram, no download. Build a gang, buy houses, hotels, factories and the port, take neighborhoods from rival gangs, fly planes and helicopters, escape the police and join the City Vault heist with other players in real time. It runs on Solana: every in-game coin is backed 1:1 by stablecoins in a public vault and players can cash out to their own wallet. Available in English, Spanish and Portuguese.

projects.title: ApexDrawn
projects.summary: Draw custom circuits, race in 3D, and build your own cars in ApexDrawn, a free browser racing game. Play online with no download required.

projects.title: Engage
projects.summary: Whether facilitating a workshop, hosting a team meeting, or leading a learning session, presenters can use games and audience participation to encourage discussion and explore different perspectives. Participants join from their phones or computers and respond to questions as the session progresses. Presenters can explore responses through visual results, review individual or team standings, and download session scores for later reference.

projects.title: YoAIRap
projects.author: YoAIRap Team
projects.summary: YoAIRap is a web-based AI rap video generator. Upload one or two photos of yourself, a friend or your pet, type what the rap is about, and get a short music video with original lyrics, a beat and vocals. Raps can be written in 35 languages. - **Create your own**: the AI writes the lyrics, picks a beat and films your photos performing the song, with sound, in 15 or 30 seconds. - **Hot templates**: remake viral rap memes such as Hotel Lobby with your own faces. Templates are silent, so add the trend's sound when you post. - Watermark-free MP4s, vertical 9:16 or wide 16:9, up to 1080p. Failed videos are refunded automatically. Pricing: Paid, from $4.99 for one standard video. Free rap lyrics, rap name, diss track and freestyle text tools are also available (daily limits apply). Official site: https://yoairap.com

projects.title: Show HN: Domino Rally – design in 2D, watch in 3D
projects.author: orgiggly-dave
projects.summary: This is a free to play, no sign up required domino rally simulator. You design them with the editor, and then run them in the 3D player. The from-behind "Chase" view is best. My mum helped develop it - she submitted issue reports direct from the app itself (make it possible to bend the domino tracks, make the playback controls disappear while mouse inactive, add like buttons to the showcase, let me change the backdrop, etc) and the Claude Code session running in the cloud watched, fixed them and on my approval, pushed them live. I've been making a lot of apps in various sessions which share the same repo. One of them https://www.orgiggly.com/david/aurora (an atmospheric musical loop generator) was plundered to generate a unique soundtrack for each rally (seeded by its name) - which is exactly how the orgiggly platform I built is supposed to work - each app created can make contributions to the next one.

projects.title: Mathing
projects.summary: Mathing is a fast, free daily mental math game. You get 60 seconds to solve as many arithmetic equations (+, −, ×, ÷) as you can. Everyone plays the exact same daily puzzle that resets at midnight, plus an unlimited practice mode to warm up or keep playing anytime. No ads, no accounts, and no app downloads—just open your browser, play in 60 seconds, and share your score.

projects.title: Card & Puzzle
projects.summary: Start a table, send the code, and play Spades, Hearts, Euchre, Crazy 8s, Gin Rummy, Rummy or Trash with friends in any browser. Phones, laptops and the app sit at the same table, and computer players fill any empty seat. Plus solitaire, Mahjong, jigsaws, Minesweeper, Cat Doku and new daily games with leaderboards. Free, no download, no account needed. Free iOS and Android apps too.

projects.title: Gridbloom: Block Puzzle Game
projects.summary: Drag, drop and clear! Gridbloom is a relaxing block puzzle game you can play anywhere. Fill rows and columns on the 8×8 board to clear them, chain combos and beat your best score in this calm, colourful brain game. Easy to learn and hard to put down, Gridbloom is a classic block puzzle with fresh ideas, great for short breaks, long trips and quiet evenings. A large, clear board on every screen, in portrait on phones and in portrait or landscape on tablets.

projects.title: 学习 Steam 和 NetFlix 优雅的揩油定价策略: 让地主老财和穷苦欠发达地区收取不同费用.
projects.author: unibrighter
projects.summary: 正如标题所见的, Steam 游戏有所谓低价区 Netflix 有所谓低价区. --- 2010 年前后,南美区的账号几乎是 steam 玩家标配. 阿根廷人在贴吧熙熙攘攘. 购买游戏省一大笔钱,让你轻松具备国际视野(收获南美同志的友谊) --- 2026 年,吃着咖喱的印度同事会安利 youtube/netflix 会员在印度的订阅价格, 他们自豪的告诉我一年可以省下 100 多澳币. “weihy node?” --- 所以 indie dev 不妨学习这些大公司的思路. 对自己的产品,不管是 app 还是 iap 或者 saas. 让地主老财和穷苦欠发达地区收取不同费用. --- 所以 写了这个插件, 后来觉得插件还是太烦, 直接上 javascript 复制到书签就能用. [用 big mac index 给你的 ios app 和 iap item 定价]( https://bigmacindex.app/app-store-pricing-advisor/) ios 进行 appstore,直接就可以自动计算了. ![全自动自动定价]( https://bigmacindex.app/videos/big-mac-pricing-fill-10s.gif) --- 总而言之,用的经济学人的大麦克指数. (其实更好的是 ppp 购买力算过来,其实国内人民币还是被刻意压低了. 根据全球贫富差距和经济水平给你的产品合理定价. 比如你可以给中东石油王爷们收取和美国一样高的费用. 同时相对的,你也可以选择狠狠压榨瑞典的骑士贵族姥爷们 (因为老爷们发部分已经习惯了什么都很贵,你的一天伙食费很可能只有他们的一杯咖啡.) 大概就是这个思路吧. 欢迎提意见和批评.

projects.title: Superior Chess Academy
projects.summary: Live online chess classes for kids, teens and adults. 1,000+ students in 20+ countries. 30,000+ hours of live coaching. Group (max 8–10), semi-private (max 3–4) and one-to-one classes. Lessons 50–60 minutes, 8 sessions a month. Real games after almost every class and a tournament every week. Free trial class on WhatsApp +91 84015 33777.

projects.title: oxom
projects.summary: OXOM is back with a redesigned experience, new branding, and the same mission: helping creators. Built for creator teams, OXOM brings collaboration, workflows, and the tools creators already use into one connected workspace. The goal isn’t to replace everything with yet another platform, but to help existing tools work better together. With the new SOCIAL feature, creators can publish content across multiple platforms. They can also use CONNECT as a team chat to stay in touch.

projects.title: Pynokio
projects.summary: Create realistic music, natural-sounding voiceovers, videos, images, and sound effects - all in one place. Explore limitless creative possibilities, maintain consistency across your projects, and bring your ideas to life faster with Pynokio.

projects.title: Grundsicherungratgeber
projects.summary: Grundsicherungratgeber explains Germany's social security benefits in clear, simple German. Step-by-step guides on Grundsicherung and Bürgergeld: who qualifies, how much you can receive, which documents you need, and how to apply — without the bureaucracy headache. Free to read for everyone who needs it.

projects.title: Dibsillion
projects.summary: “Dibs!” is now a game. Every day, 7 prompts. Name something rare and score big. Name it FIRST and it’s yours forever: your name planted on it for every player who comes after. Miss it, and someone else claims it. Free. No sign-up. 3 minutes.

projects.title: Letter4U
projects.author: reeder
projects.summary: Letter4U is a digital love-letter and memory-page maker. Choose a template, write your message, add photos and optional music or a PIN, preview in the browser, then publish a shareable link. Writing, previews and drafts are free. Official one-time publishing packs are 1 letter $1.99, 5 letters $4.99, and 15 letters $9.99 USD. No subscription. Unused purchased credits do not expire. Editing a published letter does not use another credit. It is not an AI writing tool.

projects.title: Tapfolio
projects.summary: Tapfolio keeps your social profiles and links together on your iPhone, so you can share them without searching through different apps. Show a QR code in person, copy a link for a message, or create a profile or business card with the links you choose. You can also save website links and organize your cards with folders. Free to start.

projects.title: Medimate: Pill & Med Reminder
projects.summary: Never miss a pill or a doctor's appointment again. Medimate is the only medication reminder that also tracks your appointments and works right from your Apple Watch. Most pill reminder apps only handle medications. Medimate handles your entire health routine -- medications, doctor visits, and health data -- all in one clean, simple app.

projects.title: Kappo
projects.summary: Kappo is a next-generation P2P social network and micro-economy where language barriers no longer exist. Every post, comment, and private chat is automatically translated into the reader's native language in real time. Built with an algorithmic Trust Score (0–1000 PTS), SHA-256 cryptographic authorship verification for photos and videos, and Kappo Credits (KC) to reward original creators. Zero friction, global reach.

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Harness Hollow：两个人共用一个农场的 3D 合作种田游戏，浏览器里就能玩
projects.author: KrasimirKralev

github.name: KrasimirKralev/harvest-hollow
github.description: Harness Hollow: a cozy co-op 3D farming game for two, in the browser. Play free or self-host (Node + Three.js); self-hosters get Harvey, a helper that turns a wish into a game mod.

projects.summary: 我是 Harness Hollow 的作者。这是一款两人合作的 3D 种田游戏：两个人共用同一个农场，实时一起种地、养动物、在工坊里加工产品，一个人种下的作物另一个人可以收获，双方的操作会立刻出现在彼此的屏幕上。电脑、平板和手机的浏览器都能玩，界面目前只有英文和保加利亚语。 前端是 Three.js（不用打包工具，通过 import map 加载），后端是一个很小的 Node.js 服务（Express + ws）。同一套 JavaScript 规则引擎既在浏览器里预测操作，又在服务器上做最终判定。可以用 npm install && npm start 或 Dockerfile 自己部署。 代码主要由 AI 编程助手写成（以 Claude Code 为主，OpenAI Codex 做复查），我负责设计、定方向和试玩验收；插画由 AI 图像模型生成。 在线试玩（无需注册）：

projects.title: IsDownNow
projects.summary: IsDownNow tracks public availability signals for 592 websites, apps, games, cloud platforms, ISPs and utilities, then runs in-browser latency, DNS and packet tests so you know if a disruption is widespread or just your connection.

projects.title: MetricBridge
projects.summary: MetricBridge answers questions about your Apple Health data on your iPhone, and shows the days and samples behind every answer so you can check it. It also exports 194 metrics as JSON and ships an open-source MCP server, so Claude, Cursor or a local model can read your real numbers. No account. Your health data is not sent to us or to a cloud AI. Free for 7 days, then $24.99 once.

projects.title: 【网站自荐】一把键盘，两个人怎么玩？三个可以在浏览器里直接试的合作游戏
projects.author: zhongweiv
projects.summary: 向周刊读者自荐一个适合两个人坐在同一台电脑前试的小游戏专题。我们运营 Elunvi Games，整理这页时发现，只写「支持多人」很难判断朋友能不能马上加入，真正有用的是把两个人各自要做的事、怎么加入、用哪组按键写在一起。 比如《珊瑚航海记》开局选 2，一人用 A/D 掌舵、W 提拉，另一人用上下方向键收放船帆、左右方向键稳住绳索。《钟楼奇盗》则让每人先按自己的跳跃键加入，再分工扳机关、穿过齿轮，最多可以四个人共用键盘。专题列了三款免费桌面网页游戏，每款都标明操作、人数和游戏内语言。专题有中文，游戏内语言各有不同。 共用一把键盘的合作网页游戏

projects.title: Show HN: Poker Diary, a tool to help organise your home games and track stats

projects.title: Show HN: A browser RTS where you play alongside your local agents
projects.author: fraywing
projects.summary: Howdy HN! Inspired by StarSkirmish, I wanted to build a complex RTS that required you to bring your OWN agents and either play with them as allies, against them as enemies, or battle head-to-head with other agent-human pairs in public matches. In AC you operate one or more planes (Orbit, Sky, Surface, Depths) of differing gameplay. As an old-school PC gamer I wanted the mechanics to resemble some of my favorite 90s games of yore: C&C, DungeonKeeper, Homeworld, StarCraft, and others. The idea is that you have specific objectives needed to maximize resource generation, aid in cross player support, and that a single plane cannot win independently. Outside of gameplay, from an agentic tech pov, there are some other really cool things that come with this, including: - A full specification + library to install agents into any game ( http://playerthree.gg/ ) - A networking SDK for bidirectional agent communication - Symmetric maps - Deterministic simulation - Benchmarking tools - (soon) published benchmark data Github: https://github.com/agent-command/agent-command Play now: https://agentcommand.gg/ Would love feedback and contribs if interested in RTS games and AI!

projects.title: Show HN: Host a site, content, or stream from a browser tab, served over WebRTC
projects.author: bromney
projects.summary: Site URL: https://fmrl.live Repository URL: https://gitlab.com/croatoa/fmrl This project allows you to host a website, content, and streaming from an open browser window. It gets served over WebRTC connections (or a Cloudfare turn server if that's not available). This is just a start. Any suggestions or feedback to improve usability, feature requests, etc is super welcome. This is a project I've had in mind for a while. I wanted to participate in building for a decentralized web, so I thought it would be cool if people could run a social network kind of page from their own machine, and allow them to diffuse content over a peer to peer net, independent of the typical social media giants. While this iteration is not quite that, it's a start. While the UI probably makes this super obvious, this is the first time I've used AI in coding (LLM, Claude Code). It really is some impressive machinery. The goal isn't privacy, but rather autonomy, more or less. I know there are real limitations (like a host user closing their browser) but I feel like the idea is at least slightly novel (probably because its a mediocre idea lol).. but it'll be interesting to see how it evolves. If you made it this far, thanks for the read. Hope you have a pleasant day.

The rules of the variants are not explained through the campaign so you have to play and guess as you go, I tried to make each new level surprising in its own way :) The idea came to me because along the years I've seen a surprising number of Tic Tac Toe custom rules and thought it would be cool to make a whole game out of it. I settled on 20 levels but have a ton more ideas and I'll probably add some in later updates. Surprisingly to me the hardest part was publishing an app on the App Store and Play Store (still pending because it requires 12 testers), the whole process was pretty nightmarish. Me and the modern 5.5 claude models made a base for the game that I liked, and then i went ham adding features / fixing some minor flaws (like adding claude code hooks so you recieve "telegrams" [the agent's responses], so you can review progress directly in-game). Right now, the game has basic factory features you'd expect from a game like this (build stuff, delete stuff, measure how much you're earning, basic selection tools), along with a few more.. "unexpected" features. This includes a fake in-game browser that has a wiki, fake forums, some fun bits of lore, some more lore, a LOT more lore, and a research graph that shows how many items or how much RP (research points) you'd need to unlock something, and some more QOL features. If anyone actually has this issue / want of a terminal-based game that runs alongside your agents so you don't doomscroll, do you have any suggestions, or additional ideas I could add? It's hosted on GitLab, soo, that's one additional thing i'd like to mention Thanks for reading!! snipedbywifi (p.s. first HN post lol) (p.s. p.s. there's a lot of hidden lore in the game, so.. lore-divers? you might like it?)

projects.summary: 作者自荐。把小红书、抖音、B站、公众号、微博的分享链接变成 AI 可读的文字：视频逐字稿、图片里的文字（OCR）、热门评论。仓库里有 MCP 服务器的接入配置、Python SDK / 命令行，以及 25 个 Agent Skill，可以装进 Claude Code、Cursor、OpenClaw。读取在托管服务上完成，不需要你的平台账号或 Cookie；客户端代码 MIT 开源，新账号送 10 个免费积分。 亮点 一个链接进去，出来的是 Markdown：标题、要点、逐字稿、图中文字、热门评论，Agent 可以直接接着用。 要点里引用的原话会和原文逐字核对，核对不上的不放出来；问一个问题（ask）时，帖子里没说就返回 found: false，不编。 不需要登录平台、不需要 Cookie，所以没有账号被封的风险。 每个 Skill 是一个 SKILL.md 加一个只用 Python 标准库的脚本；标 ★ 的单链接读取器不填 key 也能先看一次摘要（每个地址每天 2 次）。 长视频（网课、直播回放，最长 2 小时）按逐字稿优先读取。 链接解析（短链展开、平台识别）离线完成，免费、不需要 key；另有 LangChain、LlamaIndex 集成。

projects.author: nickdirienzo
projects.summary: Hey y'all, I'm Nick. I wanted to share a side project I started sometime last month. I really enjoy incremental games (like Cookie Clicker, Scritchy Scratchy, etc.) and wondered if I could get a coding agent to build a new one every day that I'd actually want to play. So I built an incremental game development harness with Claude Code. The first games were pretty rough, but I found that adding a few architectural invariants and automated playtesting around things like pacing and progression made a surprisingly big difference. They're now pretty fun most days. My partner and I have been playing and talking about the games each day, and after some encouragement from a teammate, I figured I'd share the experiment with the HN community. The code is available here: https://github.com/nickdirienzo/incremendle It's AGPL in part because it uses Strudel for music generation. I've also tried to be thoughtful about crediting the artists whose work inspires the games. Would love to hear what you think of this silly experiment!

projects.title: Show HN: Apron Chat Protocol
projects.author: shazow
projects.summary: Hi HN friends - I've been obsessed with chat protocols for ages - one previous project is ssh-chat ( https://ssh.chat/ ) I come bringing a new kind of chat protocol that I've been working on since I spent quite a lot of time exploring the 14 other competing standards we've come up with in the past few decades. The protocol details are here: https://apron.chat I'm hoping that Apron will better reflect our needs beyond 2026, which I expect will move more and more toward semi-private chats rather than global social networks. Come say hi on the live public demo: https://web.apron.chat Some fun facts: - The demo server runs in a Cloudflare Durable Worker. It's quite efficient, since it's hibernated except for when a message comes in. Easy to self-host this in the free tier. - Despite the JSON protocol being intentionally unabbreviated ("message" instead of "msg", etc), a typical Apron session still uses almost half as much bandwidth and messages compared to an equivalent Matrix or XMTP session. This is largely because Apron minimizes the number of roundtrips and state required for common chat scenarios. Also it compresses very nicely! - The official reference client is a PWA (Apron Web), we also have a TUI, macOS, and an iOS implementation by third party Apron-enjoyers. There's two reference server implementations (Cloudflare worker in TS and a Go implementation), plus a bunch of minimal implementations. - My favourite fun capability is embedding streaming messages, great for LLM outputs. This can be done just by piping to a curl command, no additional dependencies. There's also a mode for streaming a terminal (by piping something like `script` from util-linux which handles row/col/baud flushing, no special dependencies either). See section 4.8 for details: https://apron.chat/protocol#48-embeds-and-avatars

projects.title: Show HN: Daily Atlas, my geography quiz game where rarer answers score more
projects.author: ClozeLine
projects.summary: Hi everyone. I'm an AI Masters student (UvA Amsterdam), and quite the geography nerd, having spent countless hours on GeoGuessr. I wanted to make my own simple geography game, but with some (even small) AI component to it. The game consists of 6 geography-related questions (countries, capitals, flags, languages, borders, etc) every day, where the rarer your answer, the rarer your score (tiers are [common, uncommon, rare, ultra rare, legendary]). No account needed or anything. Something I didn't expect to cause so many issues were definitions. What counts as a country? A territory? When does a country 'speak' a language? I would set a definition, and players would always (justifiably so!) break it -> "Well OK then if this is the definition, how come you don't accept [very obscure super borderline answer]". Eventually I converged on a happy-medium with enough inclusion (I think), without the definition being a whole paragraph long: (i) Country: a sovereign state. Niue and the Cook Islands still cause problems: the UN lists them as "non-member states", but they exhibit quite a bit of sovereignty, so I count them as countries. (ii) Territory: a place with an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, given or reserved, that isn't a sovereign state (e.g., Heard Island and McDonald Islands, Sint Maarten, Sark,...) (iii) Language spoken in {country}: working or official language, as said so by the government (or the entity's governing body) Two components I think would be interesting for Show HN, and would like feedback on, are how I determine an answer's rarity and the day's difficulty. Difficulty: I trained a linear regression model on past play data (30 days, currently) to predict a number between 0 and 1. For each of the first 5 questions (the 6th is different in nature), I gather 3 features for the regression model: ln(num. possible answers), ln(1 + num. 'common' answers), and whether answers contain a 'legandary' (0 or 1), then take the weighted average. Fixed cut-offs snap that into a 1-5 difficulty level (e.g., 4/5). Rarity (e.g, "Name a country in the EU" -> Belgium): (i) Fame. Using Google Books Ngram (how often the name appears in English), QRank (pageviews of the name's wikidata item, summed over every wikipedia language), and Wikipedia page views (median yearly views), I calculate a "Fame Score" for every country, territory, and capital (e.g., USA: 7.18, France: 6.85, Tuvalu: 5.76) (ii) Weight. Sometimes rarities still don't feel quite right, so every question template (e.g., "Name a country in Europe") gets a weight based on how much information it gives the player. Luxembourg is valid for both "Name a country" and "Name a country in Europe", but knowing it's in Europe narrows your possibilities, making Luxembourg an "easier" answer for the latter. (iii) Multiply Fame times the Weight to get a rarity score from 0-100, snapped to one of the rarity tiers. It's a side project, and I'm continuously improving things based on feedback from players emailing me. Perhaps some of you could also provide some feedback? 1. How did the game 'feel' to you? 2. Were any of your answers rejected? 3. What is something you like about the game? 4. What is something you dislike about the game? 5. Any other miscellaneous observations/suggestions/bugs Anything is appreciated. Thank you for your read, and have a good day/night!

projects.title: Show HN: Klad, a paint app your coding agent can drive (source-available)
projects.author: ambewas

github.name: klad-app/klad
github.description: A drawing app built for agent/human collaboration

projects.summary: I've been developing applications for a long time and have turned to game development as well lately. One of the things that frustrated me the most was that using AI agents for game development is very annoying in the art department. Your only options right now are to either use an image genAI model and roll the dice every time you want to make an edit, or have your agent draw with something like vectors. I was looking for an application that would allow me to ask an agent to make a first draft of whatever art I needed with actual brushes, and then be able to go in myself and edit every last stroke or layer that it created. Klad is that application. Written in Rust, it can be fully controlled by an agent through the CLI, and every function is available in a nice UI as well: a brush engine, frame-by-frame animation (and bones/IK), vectors, text layers, colours, layer effects, infinite undo (even after re-opening the file!),… Why I think it's useful for a wider audience: Adobe showed agents editing Photoshop files at MAX this week, with a private beta planned for early 2027. Klad is built on the same core idea, with editable paint strokes as core architecture, and it works today. Clone the repo to try it out: https://github.com/klad-app/klad You can basically point Claude to the repo, ask it to build it, and pick up the drawing skills. Then ask it to make any drawing you want! (After that, you or the agent can change absolutely every brush stroke in the app again, which makes edits a breeze.) The quality of the drawings really depends on the agent you use. I have tried it with Claude Fable 5.2 since it came out on Monday, and the drawings are already quite impressive. I'm confident that this will only improve. I use it every day on Mac, so that definitely works well. It builds on Linux too (tablet pen pressure still needs some work there). Windows builds in CI, I haven't used it there myself yet but I have some reports that it works perfectly fine. Coming up next is support for pixel art. I'm in the testing phase with this right now, and I expect it to go live in the repo sometime this weekend. Klad is source-available rather than open source: free to build and use for individuals and small companies, and I plan to sell pre-built binaries later, the way Aseprite does. The file format, CLI reference and agent skill are MIT. What I want to hear from people who try it: Can your agent work out the CLI without help, and where does it get confused? Can you go in and change one of its strokes easily? The command reference and guides are available at https://klad.studio I'll be here answering any questions about the technical side as well, as it's a pretty interesting challenge to build a performant engine with editable brush strokes that render as paint.

projects.title: Show HN: Collection of Beauty–a walkable 3D museum of public-domain art
projects.author: trebeljahr
projects.summary: Hi HN, this is Collection of Beauty, a walkable, multi-floor 3D museum, based on a collection of art that I handpicked with 4000+ works. History: I've spent some time earlier this year just browsing Wikipedia public domain art for literally hours on end, downloading everything that I liked or appreciated, just asking myself do I find this beautiful on some level? The result is this... Well, not quite ^^ In the end I had a large folder with a bunch of images in it that begged the question: can I make this more useful somehow? Like, it's nice to have all these images sitting on my hard disk somehow but I want to share this with other people as a Collection of Beauty. But they were just images, nothing else. A bit of wrangling with AI later and now this website exists. It has a 3D museum you can walk through, with multiple floors. The images are displayed at their real sizes relative to one another and the room layouts etc. And yes, the Mona Lisa is that small ^^ Luckily Wikimedia file names can be reverse searched and therefore I had access to the entire Wikimedia metadata against each of the images to sort them and create a metadata catalogue that allows for different ways of slicing through the images, like showing things like: "similar artists", "other artists the artist knew personally", or just "epoch/style" related ideas. I also sorted paintings by color on one of the sub pages, because I thought that would be nifty. If you find something that is clearly in the wrong epoch or by the wrong artist or the wrong size, has a wrong title or whatever, please file an issue on GitHub ( https://github.com/trebeljahr/collection-of-beauty ). Also I know of this other project that did something similar (though they mapped literally all art that ever existed), but I swear I had this idea on my own, sometimes different people come up with the same stuff. https://artmuseum.artfrompixels.com/ When a friend sent this to me, I took some inspiration though and made the frames and lighting and general 3D experience much more beautiful as well. I also had to facepalm myself and whisper: "why didn't I think of this myself," and then added some (public domain or freely licensed) music playing in the background as you look at the paintings. The whole thing is deployed with Cloudflare workers because it's 90% static and Cloudflare has very very generous free tiers. Also credit where credit is due, the set of flowers from Redoute is from https://www.c82.net/redoute/ one of my favorite websites of all time ^^ Under the hood the image rendering in the 3D walkthrough does something cool with LOD texture variants where rooms determine when to load each painting's resolution based on a bunch of heuristics, keeping the experience relatively lightweight and fast (hopefully). It should load the really big scans only if you jam up your nose right into a painting. If some beautiful but more modern art is missing (MC Escher?!) then this is because of copyright issues. There are quite a few artists whose work I would love to include in here but where there is still copyright on the images and therefore I can't afaik. Also, if you have more Public Domain art, that you personally really like, please share that with me too, would love to include more stuff in here (if I like it ofc ^^). Link to Wikipedia, name of the artist to check out, name of the painting, etc.

projects.title: [网站自荐】动动乐园：打开网页、站到摄像头前就能玩的 100 多个体感小游戏，手机还能当遥控器
projects.author: zerosoul
projects.summary: 动动乐园： 100 多个体感小游戏，打开网页、站到摄像头前就能玩。不用手柄、不用装软件、不用买设备，笔记本或台式机自带的摄像头就够了，适合 3～18 岁的孩子在家里或教室里动起来。 （真实录像，用游戏自带的录像功能录制） 起因 上幼儿园中班的女儿前段时间生病，在家休养出不了门。小孩子精力旺盛，总不能天天坐着看动画片，家里又没有游戏机。手边只有一台笔记本，那就用它的摄像头：她在屏幕前跳，屏幕里的小人跟着跳；挥手切水果、蹲下躲激光、摆姿势穿墙洞……一个接一个做下来，就有了动动乐园。 能做什么 100 多个游戏，幼儿园、小学、中学都有，每个学段三档难度 中文语音带着做，不识字的小朋友也听得懂 举手就能「隔空点」按钮，站在两三米外，不用跑回电脑前 跳绳、深蹲、开合跳、高抬腿，摄像头帮你数，体育家庭作业打卡用得上 班级模式：每个孩子起个小名（不用真名），一局结束点「下一位小朋友」按名单换人，投到教室大屏上全班一起玩；每周一键生成班级运动小报 两人比赛、两人合作，好友挑战，每日小任务，奖牌和贴纸 每个账号有自己的主页，可以关注朋友、看朋友的动态 装到桌面以后，不联网也能玩 最新功能：手机当遥控器 「隔空点」对大一点的孩子很好用，可我家四岁的女儿还是常常点不准：一局玩完就站在那儿等，我只好一直守在电脑旁边。所以最近做了手机遥控器：孩子在大屏上玩，大人坐在沙发上，用手机帮她点、帮她排。 怎么连：在电脑上点右上角的手机按钮，用手机扫一下二维码就连上了。手机上不用装 App，也不用登录；链接可以随时重置。 手机上看得到：大屏正在玩哪个游戏、到了哪一步（听玩法、站位、倒数、开玩、看成绩）、这一局还剩几秒、拿了几颗星。 手机上能做的： 1. 替孩子点按钮：大屏上此刻能点的「开始」「再玩一次」「下一位小朋友」，手机上同步出现，点一下就行；也能暂停、跳过、回到选游戏。 2. 排一张游戏单：从收藏的、最近玩的或全部游戏里挑几个排进去，可以调到最前、拿掉。一局玩完，大屏过几秒自己接着玩下一个。游戏单存在大屏那台电脑上，手机锁屏了、断网了，大屏照样一个接一个玩下去。 3. 不想挑也行：点一张现成的游戏单——「早起热身」「坐久了动一动」「放学放放电」「体能练一练」「动动脑」「睡前静一静」，或者点「帮我排 10 分钟」，大屏按孩子的年龄自己挑好。排好的可以存成常用游戏单，下次一点就换上，连名字都不用打。 4. 定好玩多久：比如定 20 分钟。到点不会把正在玩的这一局掐断，等这一局玩完，大屏才盖上「今天玩够啦，休息一下眼睛，喝口水」。孩子求情的话，手机上点「再玩 5 分钟」。 5. 发一句鼓励：「你真棒！」「再坚持一下！」「玩完这一局，就来吃饭啦」……大屏上弹出来，还会读给孩子听。 6. 静音、换难度也能在手机上点（难度等这一局玩完再换）。 连着遥控器的时候，大屏顶上会挂一个小小的手机图标和一闪一闪的绿点，不挡游戏。教室里也一样好用：老师拿着手机站在孩子们中间点「下一位小朋友」，不用每次走回讲台。 遥控器只传文字：在玩哪个游戏、还剩几秒、几颗星。手机上看不到摄像头画面，这是特意这么设计的。 隐私 摄像头画面只在你自己的电脑上处理，不上传；录像也只存在这台电脑上，除非你自己点了存到云相册。大人登录以后同步的只有成绩、名单这些数据，不含画面。 免费和会员 不登录可以先试玩两局，登录后免费账号每天也有几局可以玩。会员（家庭版、班级版、学校版）不限局数，另外有手机遥控器、云相册、AI 成长报告和会员装扮，价格见 。 怎么玩 1. 电脑用 Chrome 或 Edge 打开 ，点「开始玩」 2. 离摄像头 2～3 米，从头到脚都进画面（第一次玩可以先做一下「设备检测」，一分钟查完摄像头、光线和站位） 3. 动起来！接上电视或投影更带劲 到现在前后发了快 100 个版本，游戏难度按孩子们真实玩下来的成绩调过。之前在 V2EX 介绍过一次（ ），这次主要加了手机遥控器。欢迎带娃来试试，有问题可以在网站里点「意见反馈」，我都会看。

projects.title: Show HN: Move more with short random exercise challenges
projects.author: brendanperry
projects.summary: Background: I've been working on Sporadic for years, while software engineering has been my full-time job. That means this code is mine, and I know it well since it was built in the pre-AI era. However, AI has allowed me to expand the features to a place where I am more confident in sharing it. Why: As an engineer, I sit and look at a screen all day. My brother is a graphic designer and does the same. Our goal was to build an app to get us on our feet, and one where we could do it together. What makes Sporadic fun is a mix of short exercises at random times during your day that you can do with your friends. We've got stats, streaks, and community-wide daily challenges. The mix of social accountability, random timing of challenges, and a streak to hold onto make it an effective tool for convincing me to do some push-ups between meetings. How it works: Get a push notification to do a specific short exercise within a given time limit. These can also be done with friends, and you'll get a push when they complete one. A buddy doing the challenge is an incredible motivator. Tech: I started this project long ago to learn Swift and SwiftUI. The project is decidedly Apple, with a CloudKit database on the back end. One really cool thing this gives me is the ability to have an authenticated user based on their iCloud account only, so you don't have to create an account to use Sporadic and join up with friends. Otherwise, CloudKit is pretty frustrating to use, and it will make it more difficult to add support for Android. If there is any Android demand, please let me know! Conclusion: I've enjoyed using Sporadic myself and hope that someone else out there could benefit from it. I would love some feedback on what is good and what needs improved. Thanks for reading.

github.description: 轮盘式窗口快速切换工具

projects.summary: ShaiZero 是一个 Windows 窗口切换器，只做一件事：在你鼠标当前所在的位置，弹出一个轮盘，让你直接选窗口。按住触发键（默认 Alt + 鼠标左键，可改成鼠标侧键或其他组合），轮盘就在指针处展开；指针停在哪一格松手，哪个窗口就到前台，拖回圆心或点右键取消。你不需要把鼠标移向任务栏，也不需要打开 Alt+Tab 列表再逐格扫描——窗口切换这个动作，被压缩成一次“在指针原地转一下手腕”。 为什么值得推荐 日常切窗口的惯性路径是：手离开工作区 → 鼠标奔向任务栏 → 在缩略图/图标里辨认 → 点击。窗口一多，这条路径就变成反复的视觉搜索和手部位移，节奏被打断得零碎。 ShaiZero 的做法是把“选择”搬回你鼠标已经在的地方。轮盘在指针处弹出，候选窗口环绕在圆心周围，哪一格对应哪个窗口一目了然；指针从圆心滑向目标扇区、松手即完成切换。整个过程鼠标不需要大范围移动，眼睛也不需要离开当前工作区去任务栏上做二次辨认。 更关键的是，触发键不绑定在某一个固定方案上。设置里可以直接点方框，按你想用的鼠标侧键或任意键作为触发键。对习惯用侧键的人来说，切窗口可以做到“拇指一按、指针一滑、松手到位”，手几乎不用离开鼠标当前位置。轮盘半径、扇区间距、动画、主题也都可调，呼出方式支持任意单键、组合键或鼠标侧键。 这个交互的灵感，来自游戏里的轮盘系统 ShaiZero 的轮盘不是一个凭空发明的桌面控件，它的手感直接来自几款游戏里已经被验证过的交互设计： 《Apex 英雄》的 Ping 轮盘：按住 Ping 键，轮盘在屏幕上展开，移动鼠标选信号，松开即发送。ShaiZero 把“按住 → 轮盘出现 → 指向目标 → 松手确认”这套长按手势 + 径向菜单的节奏，原样搬到了窗口切换上。 《英雄联盟》的信号轮盘：长按 G 或 Alt，八向轮盘在指针位置展开，选信号松手即发出。轮盘贴着鼠标位置出现、而非固定在屏幕中央或角落——ShaiZero 沿用了这一空间逻辑。 《三角洲行动》的快捷轮盘：长按数字键呼出药品/物品轮盘，在战斗中实现“不离开战斗视野”的快速选择。这套设计的目标正是减少手部位移和注意力切换，与 ShaiZero 想解决的桌面窗口切换问题同构。 你已经在游戏里练出了“肌肉记忆级”的轮盘操作；ShaiZero 让你在桌面上复用同一套手感。 技术上也足够省心 单个 exe，绿色免安装，不需要 .NET / VC++ 运行库，不需要管理员权限，Windows 10 1809+ 或 Windows 11 x64 即可运行。

projects.title: 做了个在线去人声的工具，从原曲里拆出伴奏和人声两轨
projects.author: catlovefishing
projects.summary: KTV 伴奏大多是重新翻录的，跟原版听着差不少。想要原版的伴奏，就只能从原曲里把人声去掉，所以做了这个。人声也单独给一轨，可以拿来对歌词、听换气。 https://www.voiceremover.app/ 前端是 TypeScript + React + TanStack Start ，整个跑在 Cloudflare Workers 上，D1 存数据，R2 放文件，排队用 Queues 。分离模型用的 htdemucs ，跑在 fal 上，混音和转 MP3 放在 Cloudflare 那边做。一首歌一般半分钟左右出结果，两轨都能在页面上先听，跟原曲对比着听完再下载。 传视频（ MP4/MOV ）的话，浏览器会先在本地把音轨抽出来，只上传音频，手机拍的大视频也传得动。 同一套分离另外开了两个入口。提取人声那个默认先放干声，给做 remix 的人用。去背景音乐那个是保留说话声、去掉音乐，vlog 、播客、采访录音里混进了歌可以用它处理。 免费每天 1 首完整的歌，不用注册，登录后每天 2 首，导出 MP3 ，没水印。付费是 Pro $4.99/月，最多 120 首；或者一次性 $3.99 买 15 首，不过期。 现在的问题：人声混响很重的歌、观众跟着一起唱的现场版、老的单声道录音，伴奏里还会残留一点人声。和声、伴唱会跟主唱分在一起，拆不开。界面目前只有英文和日文，中文还没做。 有分离效果不好的歌可以丢过来，我拿去看看问题出在哪。

As a semi-retired developer now playing with the new tools of the trade, I put this together (aka iterated with Claude over 12 weeks and about 300 km of runs), and this is what came out. The biggest challenges were getting the zoom levels and transitions right as you race against up to 6 past versions of you and different performances, as well as the map detail in a way that would work for both road and trail runs. I'm proud of it and would love for some of you to test it as well and have fun with it.

You can view it via the website. :P Release Blogpost: https://sadale.net/en/86/ Github (Scrolldown for English): https://github.com/SadaleNet/ilo-musi-8 Devlog: https://forum.frutigeraeroarchive.org/viewtopic.php?t=1371 Website: https://ilomusi8.sadale.net/en/welcome

projects.title: Show HN: Thousand Suns, a nuclear war sandbox
projects.author: gxd
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm the author of Thousand Suns (1KS). This has been my full-time project for the past six months and is now available as freeware for Windows, Linux and macOS (experimental) on itch.io. It started as a game but slowly turned into a serious simulation as I educated myself on nuclear war. I'm a stay-at-home dad, previously a Big Tech software engineer, and not a nuclear war expert. But I spent an enormous amount of time learning about the subject from original and derived sources, such as the well-known site NUKEMAP. It goes beyond existing free projects by simulating full conflicts on top of single detonations. The conflicts are “all out” and meant to be a demonstration of the power of present-day arsenals rather than a depiction of nuclear war escalation. This was made with Godot/C# and I spent a good amount of time hand-optimizing the code... Not because it was needed, but because it was fun! I'm not using any external libraries with the exception of Godot itself. It was all custom-made and the nuclear calculations were derived from the amazing 1977 book "The Effects of Nuclear Weapons" by Glasstone and Dolan. I decided to make it free because I think it's important to raise visibility on what is, perhaps, the most dangerous threat to our survival. Without minimizing the many other risks we face, it is the one way civilization as we know it could end tonight. Feel free to ask any questions and I hope 1KS is useful for you!

projects.title: Show HN: An API for word timestamps from speech, 75% within 20ms
projects.author: jasperstory
projects.summary: Hey HN, we're Yarn (W24) and we make a video editing app for startups, and we built Quebec ( https://quebec.yarn.so ), an API that gives you accurate word timestamps from speech. We needed it because cutting a word even 50ms off from its true timing can ruin talking head footage (examples in the write up). Accurate word timestamps usually come from a forced aligner, which takes the speech audio and a transcript and works out exactly when each word starts and ends. We weren't satisfied with the accuracy of Montreal Forced Aligner (MFA) or new models like ElevenLabs Cue ( https://elevenlabs.io/blog/cue-aligner ). Giving LLMs access to a waveform/spectrogram didn't help much either. So we built our own. There are two particularly interesting parts: - We wrote our own decoder around MFA's acoustic model that only lets each word land within 200ms of the rough timings. That made search small enough to solve exactly, so we don't need to use MFA's beam search. - We added a small CNN, built on the first two layers of Whisper Tiny, that nudges each word boundary by up to 50ms. We couldn't find enough hand-labelled speech that allowed for commercial use, so we had Gemini label our own (17k word boundaries). It took a couple of hours and cost under $200. A net trained on Gemini's labels scored the same as one trained on human labels (73.9% vs. 74%). One way to measure accuracy is % of word boundaries within 20ms of hand labels. Here are the results on Buckeye (hand-labelled American speech that we didn't train on): - Quebec 75% - MFA 61% - ElevenLabs Cue 30% If you want to try it, it's free until tomorrow night. You can point your agent at our docs at https://quebec.yarn.so , and send audio on its own or with your own transcript. After that, it costs $0.32 per hour with no signup (minimum $10 top-up). We serve it at cost. Caveats: only tested in English and slower than ElevenLabs. Let us know if Quebec works well for you, and send us any samples that work badly (you can email support at yarn dot so). Also let us know if you've built or found a better aligner. In theory we would just switch to a better aligner, although we would probably just push a bit harder to make ours better. Thanks! Jasper

projects.title: Show HN: Darkroomfinder.org – A Directory of Photography Darkrooms
projects.author: stokesj84
projects.summary: I built darkroomfinder.org, a directory of photography darkrooms, as a React single page app (SPA), because I wanted to understand how SPAs work and I wanted to scale to hundreds or thousands of cities without managing routes and pages for each of them. The site currently lists over 350 darkrooms across over 50 countries. However in deciding to build a SPA I failed to realize the downsides of SPAs for SEO. As an SPA darkroomfinder.org only has one route, i.e. darkroomfinder.org. Therefore GoogleBot only indexes the root domain and if someone searches for "Darkrooms" the site might surface in Google Search, but if a user searches "San Francisco Darkrooms" Google Search is much less likely to return darkroomfinder.org as nothing indicates the site has information about San Francisco. Solving this SEO problem while maintaining the simplicity of the SPA turned out to be a challenge but I think I have arrived at a solution that checks most of the desired boxes at the cost of being tied more closely to Cloudflare's infrastructure. Cloudflare, the DNS and CDN for darkroomfinder.org, has a serverless primitive, Cloudflare Workers. These Cloudflare Workers are distributed at the edge, have KV caches, and can intercept specific paths. So my solution to having both an SPA and indexable city routes is to have Cloudflare Workers cache the city data and intercept city routes directed at darkroomfinder.org returning an HTML page with the city data and the full React SPA which boots over the HTML page. So technically it's one SPA served to many routes. GoogleBot in traversing one of these city routes, like darkroomfinder.org/san-francisco, will index the HTML page while humans using browsers receive the same HTML which the React SPA boots over. Part of the project that remains unsolved is data collection and validation. Darkroom discovery is automated by agents running daily scans for unlisted darkrooms. But a human still has to validate that the discovered darkrooms exist and try to determine what capabilities they have such as B&W or color developing etc. I am currently working on an automated reachability and vitality checker to determine if the darkrooms already in the directory are still active, since photography darkrooms sometimes cease operations long before taking down their websites or social feeds. darkroomfinder.org

projects.title: Show HN: DeployAngel – A verdict in ~20 minutes if a deploy broke production
projects.author: jkowens
projects.summary: Hey there, I'm looking for feedback on a release verification tool I'm building. https://www.deployangel.com I decided to build this after an issue popped up with a recent Rails upgrade. We upgraded a Rails app to 8.1 and picked up a new default that changes the order after_commit callbacks run. Our upload code started telling the virus scanner about files before they were saved to S3, and the scanner just quietly dropped them. No exceptions were raised and uploads sat in "processing" for days. We should have had alarms in place, we know that now but I wondered if there could be some type monitoring that would just have noticed the change. I did some checking and the callback route went from roughly 27 requests an hour to zero when we deployed. That seems like a fairly easy change in behavior to automatically raise an alarm. So after a few weekends working with Claude I have a new tool. A small agent sends one aggregated payload per minute. Then the server compares each release with the last one it cleared. It looks at things like error rates, latency per route, traffic that collapses, and missing job runs. The server then returns a verdict if the release cleared or not. Currently I have agents for Rails, Django, FastAPI, and ASP.NET Core. It will work best for teams that deploy often and the app gets steady traffic. It's not meant to replace error monitoring tools like Sentry, but to work alongside them. Here's a recent release of its own: https://app.deployangel.com/share/KAaurrfRHcw43ZrjkWst2DLY?r... The agents are MIT-licensed. It's completely free right now, with a free tier planned. https://github.com/DeployAngel I'm looking for a few teams to run it on a real app for a couple of weeks. I'd love to hear if it surfaces issues that other monitoring and alarms miss. Of course I'm hoping it proves to be useful, but if not, that's good information too.

projects.author: justswim
projects.summary: Hi HN, I’m Eric and I’m building Lettercamp, an open-source static blog framework. The repo is at https://github.com/lettercamp/lettercamp and the homepage is online at https://www.lettercamp.com . Writing good content has always been the #1 way that I’ve grown the reach of products I’ve worked on in the past. However, it’s always bothered me how many little things get in the way of writing and publishing high quality, first party content onto the web. Building a performant, SEO-optimized blog from scratch was always distracting from development on the actual product, and setting up a 3rd party CMS meant that my content always lived in someone else’s database. Storing content in a non-markdown format also made it difficult to draft and edit with the help of an AI agent. Lettercamp is a modern approach to creating a content site. It ships with all the little features you’d expect in a blog: pagination, authors, metadata, search, cross linking, related posts and more. It’s also statically built, which means that all your content lives in markdown in your codebase, so a deployed version is performant with no database to maintain. This means that you can focus on writing good content instead of vibe-coding a whole blog. I want to add more features to the framework over time, including better support for AI agents, built in localization, email sign ups, and more. The repo is released under the MIT license so that anyone can use the framework to create a content site. The goal isn’t to charge individual developers. The monetization path is to provide a cloud hosted version, that has an online editor that content teams can use. The main advantage of this is to decouple the blog from product deploys, so that teams can publish content without needing to push code. I would love to get your feedback on if this is a problem that might resonate with you or your team. I know that a lot of products create a /blog section at some point, and I wonder what solutions people are using today. My hope is that over time, Lettercamp can be the go-to solution for teams looking to set this up. Try it out: https://github.com/lettercamp/lettercamp and let me know what you think!

projects.title: 我做了一个不太一样的记账 App：它把个人财务变成了一场自己的「金融市场」
projects.author: lidinghui
projects.summary: 有时候，我觉得自己的钱挺神秘的。 明明工资按时到账，也没买什么特别贵的东西，但每个月总有那么几天，打开银行 App ，看着余额陷入沉思： 钱呢？ 我试着回忆这个月买过什么，脑子里只有几杯咖啡、几顿外卖和一些当时觉得很需要的东西。 单笔看起来都没什么问题，合起来就不太对劲了。 ![图片 2]( https://i.imgur.com/gnoLd1I.png) 我们每天都在记录这些变化，只不过大多数记账 App 最后给我们的，还是一张张账单和几个统计数字。 所以，我决定试着做点不一样的东西。 于是我开始想：如果能像看股票行情一样，看看自己的钱每天都发生了什么变化，会不会有意思得多？ 最开始只是一个想法：既然股票有行情，为什么自己的账户不能也有？ 于是，我开始把个人财务和金融市场的一些概念结合起来。 这就是 PFEx 的由来。 它本质上是一个记账 App ，不过有点不一样。 在 PFEx 里，每个账户都有自己的 K 线，可以观察余额走势、成交量和变化趋势。多个账户汇集起来，又会形成一条整体资产曲线。 收入、支出和账户间转账会被分别处理，资金流向也能通过桑基图直观呈现。除此之外，还有周期预算、专项计划、账户表现、龙虎榜和 AI 生成的财务研报。 如果不想自己翻数据，也可以直接和对话 Agent 聊天。查账、分析资金变化，甚至让它协助记录交易。当然，涉及账务修改时，仍然需要经过你的确认。 我甚至给自己的钱安排了一个研究部。 当然，我并不是想把生活变成一场股票交易，也不希望以后买杯奶茶都要先做一份投资分析。 真正有意思的，是看清自己的钱发生了什么变化，以及这些变化背后的习惯、欲望和选择。 毕竟，研究市场是为了理解别人的公司，研究自己的钱，大概是为了少一些月底看余额时的困惑。 如果你也觉得这个想法有点意思，欢迎试试，也欢迎告诉我你的看法。 官网： https://greyglow.cn/pfex/ Google Play： https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=pfex.greyglow.cn

projects.title: Show HN: Zeus – Claude Code for AI voice agents
projects.author: kolchinski
projects.summary: Hey, Alex here, I'm one of the founders. We've built phone agents for enterprise customers for two years and kept seeing the same failure: agents that mishear callers and then do something confidently wrong. We're announcing two things in this launch. #1 is the stack: instead of one transcription model → one LLM → one TTS, most conversation turns runs through several transcription models and LLMs (a fast and a slow LLM in the same call, models switched per turn, audio sent straight to an LLM alongside transcripts). That gets us 99.4% on Big Bench Audio. That's the second-highest published score; the only model above us takes almost 9 seconds to start talking as far as we've measured, which doesn't work on a phone call. Eval set and transcripts are on Hugging Face - http://huggingface.co/datasets/kolchinski/bba-storm-eval #2 is Zeus, an agent that configures our voice AI stack per use case and per conversation. We tried doing this with Claude Code and Codex and they were bad at it: they can't run simulated calls out of the box, don't do well with audio input and spotting problems in calls, and tend to blindly believe vendor marketing about which model is best vs actually trying the models. Zeus has evals on real calls, can simulate calls in hard situations, and listens to production calls to find problems, so it can check its own work the way a coding agent runs tests to make sure the code it wrote actually works. Pricing is cost-plus (vendor prices + hosting + a 17–25% margin), no subscription. Zeus is free for now. You can try it with a free $10 credit. Happy to answer questions.

projects.title: Show HN: Pots – Open-source Grok Bot alternative, used by 6 startups for a month
projects.author: Crokily
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Crokily. Pots is an AI coworker that lives in the chat your team already uses: Slack, Discord, Telegram, or any channel with a Chat SDK adapter. It is MIT-licensed and runs on a machine you give it, with the model you choose. To be honest, the first time I used Grok Bot, its design really impressed me. Unlike OpenClaw before it, it was not just Claude Code connected to a chat app. It truly cared about how it works with people. It felt like a living AI assistant, and working with it was painless. That is the idea I kept learning from the whole time I built Pots: it is not an agent hooked up to a chat channel. It should be a coworker that feels alive and is comfortable to work with. But Grok Bot is only Grok's bot. Which model you get depends on your X subscription, your data and your machine are all in the cloud, and most of all, it is a standalone app, and most of its features serve that app. Pots is a bit different. In Sydney I have talked with quite a few founders. Grok Bot is good, and it helps them a lot with their personal tasks. But when I asked who had actually put Grok Bot into their company's work to make their startup team faster, nobody had. So I think Pots is in a different place from Grok Bot, and from most open-source Grok Bot alternatives: it grew out of what real startup teams need. Before I open-sourced it, 6 small startups I met at startup events had been using it with me for over a month. Pots is built first for the channels startup teams already work in, not for an app of its own, so most of what it does serves the places where you actually work. The teams use Pots as a middle layer: a CEO talks ideas through with the team in chat, Pots listens, and then it builds a prototype that both sides can check. They use Pots for competitor research: because Pots runs inside their channels, it knows their product well. Not only the GitHub repo, but the team's daily discussions and what the team cares about. Pots has been listening quietly the whole time, so it knows the product with no setup at all. It also works well with each channel: it talks to people with the channel's own controls, like Slack and Discord buttons and cards, and when it hands over something complex, it deploys a page with its built-in server so everyone sees it in a better form. So Pots is different from Grok Bot and from most open-source alternatives. It came out of what real startup teams need. Its channel features start from what each company's work needs, and it can join your real work setup with no setup and still do well, instead of being one more app that nobody uses and that is hard to start with. And it ran in real business for a while before I cleaned it up and open-sourced it. The difference from Grok Bot is also exactly why I made Pots an open-source Grok Bot alternative. I have OpenAI and Claude subscriptions with plenty of quota, and my own servers, so I don't want an X subscription to limit me. I want to use whatever model I want and do whatever I want. I can even switch to an open model, and none of my data goes into anyone's pocket. Try it (Node 24+, macOS, Linux or Windows): the easiest way is to ask your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) to read docs/for-agents.md in the repo and set up Pots for you. Or by hand: npm install -g pi-durable-bot, then pots init. I'd love feedback, especially on how it decides when to act.

projects.title: [开源推荐] AgentFlow：Docker 一键私有化部署的 AI Agent 平台
projects.author: PHclaw

github.name: PHclaw/agentflow
github.description: 自托管 AI Agent 平台：拖拽式工作流 + 知识库 RAG + 23 个预置技能，默认 SQLite 单机可跑，一条 docker compose 私有化部署。Self-hosted, OpenAI-compatible.

projects.summary: 一个自托管的 AI Agent 平台：在浏览器里拖拽连几个节点、填几行提示词，就能把大模型、内部文档和常用工具拼成能干活儿的助手。默认两个容器加一个 SQLite 文件，不依赖 PostgreSQL 和 Redis，一条 docker compose 命令跑起来，数据存在自己硬盘上。适合数据不能出内网、又没有专职运维的中小团队；代码量适中，也适合拿来读源码。 亮点 1. 部署成本低到能塞进一台小机器 两个容器（后端 + nginx）加一个 ./data/agentflow.db 就是全部，docker compose up -d --build 完成部署，备份等于打包 data/ 目录。同类自托管方案起步通常要 PostgreSQL + Redis + worker，四五个容器。 2. 产物是真文件，不是一段文字 生成的 xlsx / png / pdf 作为附件回传，图片类直接内联渲染在对话里，不用先下载再看。这一点和多数「只回文本」的方案差别明显。 3. 换模型不用重启，已入库的向量也不会失效 任意 OpenAI 兼容端点（含本地 Ollama），界面里保存即生效。embedding 端点独立配置——换对话模型不影响向量库，不用重新入库。很多同类产品把这两个绑在一起，换模型等于重建知识库。 4. 技能就是目录 加一个带 SKILL.md 的文件夹就多一个能力，仓库自带 26 个（Excel 表格、PPT 生成、PDF 处理、学术检索、会议纪要、统计分析…），扩展不需要改任何代码。 5. 工作流引擎自研，节点状态实时回传 没有用 LangGraph——需求就六类节点（触发器 / LLM / 知识库 / 工具 / 条件 / 回复），引框架反而多一层调试成本。自研的好处是画布上的节点会逐个点亮，用户能看见跑到哪一步。 适合初学者学什么 后端 FastAPI + SQLAlchemy 2.0 async，前端 React 18 + ReactFlow，代码量适中，读源码能学到几条完整链路： SSE 流式输出：为什么不用 EventSource（不能带 Authorization 头），改用 fetch + ReadableStream 后怎么按帧解析 向量检索落地：文档解析 → 分块 → 调 embedding 端点 → 存 chromadb → 检索注入上下文，一整条 RAG 链路 把 LLM 应用做成可部署产品：Alembic 迁移与 createall 的顺序坑、JWT 鉴权、限流、Docker 多阶段构建 原生打包：用 Capacitor 把同一个 Web 前端打成安卓 App，下载逻辑怎么从 换成 Filesystem + Share 已知限制 没有异步任务队列（长任务会占住请求），权限只有「用户 / 管理员」两档，pgvector 路径未做端到端验证。定位是小团队自用，不适合高并发场景。

projects.title: Show HN: Revix AI – PR review against the standards your repo follows
projects.author: oscarestudillom
projects.summary: Hello, I’m Oscar. I’ve been leading dev teams from Barcelona with my cofounder Uri for a long time. We pushed the use of AI a lot, allowing an increase in the code shipment velocity, but our job as seniors moved from building to just reviewing. We also started to see a lot of drift in how devs were doing the code, less standards, less control, which caused more bugs and differences between what product department asked and what we shipped. It was impossible for us to keep reviewing everything by hand, so we decided to clone how we review as humans into a product: Revix AI. In easy words, Revix main strength is that it extracts from your repo all the good practices and team standards, then on every pull request comments if anything moves from that. That, paired with PR status badges and targeted notifications allowed us to reduce review time by 54% on many teams, while increasing the confidence and reducing bugs on production. We know there are other similar products around and they work fine, but we found that they trust too much on the LLM and focus just on bug hunting. Our philosophy goes further, we created a system that reviews the same as a senior engineer would do, not catching just bugs. We achieved to comment only on things devs actually fix and stop the noise. Revix AI works on GitHub, Gitlab, Bitbucket and can sync with many other tools like Slack, Jira, Linear etc. Please feel free to request any other tool that we still do not support. We offer free reviews for any open source project, and for companies we do price per seat including a 14 days free trial. If you want to see Revix AI working, you can check this example PR: https://github.com/revix-app/fastapi-revix/pull/1 And here is one from an open source project that use many other reviewers so you can compare: https://github.com/ontogr/ontogr-agent-memory/pull/19 We want to work very closely with the community, so feel free to try it out and give us feedback, we love to keep improving and listen to all the customers and developers that try our tool.

projects.summary: AGASTHY： 一个开源的桌面应用，把整台开发机连成一张图：本机的 Git 仓库（包括未提交的改动）、各语言运行时（哪个 python / node 真正生效，哪些被遮蔽了）、Homebrew / npm / pip 等装的包、AI 工具和 MCP 服务器，全部关联到一张知识图谱里，每条信息都注明来源。 几个主要功能： 删除前先看影响：比如卸载 openssl@3，会列出哪些项目会坏、哪些会退回到另一个已安装的版本，并给出恢复方法。 AI 编程 Agent 面板：同时开着 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Gemini CLI、Hermes 时，看每个会话占多少内存、启动了哪些 MCP 服务器和 dev server，以及 Agent 退出后还在跑、还占着端口的进程。 Token 用量：从各 Agent 自己的本地日志读取（只读计数，不读对话内容），按天、项目和模型统计，并按 API 公开价格估算成本。 安全清理：只清理被 Git 忽略、可以重新生成的目录（nodemodules、target 等），先移进可恢复的隔离区；任何操作都先 dry run，确认后才执行。 做它是因为同时跑多个编程 Agent 以后，机器上多了很多看不见的东西：没人关的 dev server、每个几百 MB 的 Agent 进程、重复的依赖和缓存。我的 Mac 上同时开着 6 个 Claude Code 会话，一共占了 1.7 GB 内存。现有工具要么只管磁盘，要么只看进程，没有一个能说清这些东西之间的关系，以及删掉某个东西会影响什么。 它也能给 Agent 用：自带只读的命令行工具和 MCP 服务器（9 个工具），Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、OpenClaw、Hermes 可以直接问「哪些项目有未提交的改动」「3000 端口被谁占了」「这周 Agent 花了多少 token」。 本地优先：不需要账号，没有遥测，数据只存在本机的一个 SQLite 文件里。Rust + Tauri，Apache-2.0 协议。主要支持 macOS（Apple 芯片），Windows 和 Linux 是预览版。README 顶部有一分钟的演示视频。 我是作者。

projects.title: Show HN: Belay – formal verification for SQLite migrations and queries in Lean 4
projects.author: neprotivo
projects.summary: Hi, I'm Tzanko and I'm the author of Belay. Belay is a Lean 4 library for doing formal verification of SQLite queries and migrations. It implements a semantic model of a subset of SQLite, validated by differential tests that compare the output against native SQLite. With Belay I wanted to see how difficult it is to use formal verification for everyday development tasks. It turns out it can be made not much harder than writing an integration test: you state the claim, the agent writes the proof, and Lean's kernel checks it, so the only thing you have to read is the claim (longer write-up on the motivation and agent workflow: https://vihren.dev/blog/20261112-belay/ ). While a migration is being written, your agent can run #sql_check, which searches small databases for counterexamples to a claim, and is as easy to run as a linter. Once the migration is settled, the agent writes a proof of the claims you need, for example that the migration preserves the results of existing queries and succeeds on valid data. Currently Belay supports a subset of SQLite 3.51.0, cross-checked against native SQLite on 5,768 differential test cases, most of which come from SQLite's own test suite. Unsupported SQL is rejected with a reason and never approximated. Not every rule of the model has had a human audit yet. The model covers single-connection operational semantics only: it says nothing about query plans, locks, concurrency or crash behavior. I think this approach can make formal verification as routine as testing, though two things stand in the way. The first is coverage: the model has to cover the full semantics of SQLite and all of its recent versions, and the same work has to be done for other engines such as PostgreSQL and ClickHouse. The second is proof cost: the proofs of common claims are still long for the agent to write, and they have to become short. I'm looking for design partners who want this for their workloads on SQLite or other open-source databases, because a real workload is the best guide to what to cover first. The models that come out of that work become part of Belay as open source. Reach out at contact@vihren.dev. If you know a tricky SQLite edge case where the model might diverge from native SQLite, or a gnarly migration bug you've hit in production, I'd love to test it and hear your thoughts.

projects.summary: Project URL Category Python Project Title clx: switch AI coding accounts without restarting Project Description clx is a Linux launcher for Anthropic's coding CLI. It starts each session on whichever of your own Pro/Max accounts has the most usage left. At its 5-hour or weekly limit, clx moves the running session to your next account without a restart. Highlights Unlike switchers that pick an account only at launch, clx also moves a session that is already running. The conversation, background tasks and subagents carry on; only the login used by the next request changes. At launch it compares every window the server reports (5-hour, weekly and per-model) and picks the account with the most room. One standard-library Python file, a bash hook and an installer. SECURITY.md lists every file it writes and the one request it makes, and --uninstall removes it. It is for accounts that are all yours. The README has a "Use it within Anthropic's terms" section; sharing an account is forbidden. I'm the author of clx. Example Code bash curl -fsSL | tar xz ./clx/install.sh cm-login work you@work.example # log in a second account, named work clx --status # every account, its usage, and which one clx would pick clx # start on the account with the most room Screenshots or Demo Videos

github.name: AIE-enginehub/Oryh
github.description: Headless, AI-native ERP & CRM built for AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, MCP). Software keeps the ledger; agents run the workflow.

projects.summary: 自荐一个我们刚在 GitHub 开源的项目 Oryh（Apache-2.0，FastAPI + SQLAlchemy + PostgreSQL + React 管理台）： GitHub 2 分钟实机演示（YouTube）： 线上体验： （国内）/ （海外） 为什么做 Oryh？ 市面上很多 AI ERP/CRM 是在传统表单界面旁边加了一个聊天框，结果 Agent 反而要花大量上下文去适配既有的界面字段和写死的状态机。Oryh 选择了相反的分工：软件只负责把账记老实、守住权限与数据边界，业务判断与推进全部交给 AI Agent。 三个核心设计： 1. Agent 就是业务前端：没有日常业务录入页面，员工直接用自己惯用的 Claude Code、Codex、OpenClaw、Hermes 或任意 MCP 客户端，用自然语言完成报工时、贴发票报销、拟报价单、核对采购三单匹配、预留库存并过账发货；React Console 仅保留给管理员做团队配置、权限管控和审计回看。 2. 业务规则是带版本的自然语言，而不是 if/else：审批流、折扣红线、数据校验规范以纯文本形式存储在版本化、带生效日期的 businessrules 表中，流程位置由只追加的 approvalrecords 与 todos 实时推导——调整审批路线只需对管理员 Agent 说一句话，无需改代码或重新发布。 3. 零 SDK 的 SKILL.md + HTTP（并原生内置 OAuth 2.1 POST /mcp）：员工本地 Agent 通过浏览器 Device Flow（oryh-connect）授权一次，即可自动拉取与其 RBAC 角色严格匹配的 Markdown 技能包和 OpenAPI 契约；服务端通过 PostgreSQL Row-Level Security（RLS）、不可篡改明细账本及账期锁定兜底，确保 Agent 无论怎么理解上下文都无法越权写坏账。 单租户完整功能开箱自托管（docker compose up -d --build，支持可选执行 scripts/seedsample.py 一键加载虚构公司样例数据进行体验）。欢迎大家体验和指正！

projects.summary: 大家好，自荐一下我自己做的开源项目：Tabrelay，让脚本和 AI Agent 直接操作你自己已经登录好的 Chrome。 开源仓库： （Python + Chrome 扩展，MIT，免费） 介绍页和使用指南： 起因：我想让 AI Agent 帮我操作网页，但不想再开一个自动化浏览器、重新登录一遍、过一遍两步验证，有些网站还会把自动化浏览器当机器人。所以我写了这个：一个很小的 Chrome 扩展加一个 Python 文件，命令行把任务（打开页面、执行 JS、点击、输入、上传文件、截图）通过 127.0.0.1 发给扩展，扩展用 Chrome DevTools Protocol 在你日常用的 Chrome 里执行。 用你真实的浏览器：你的 profile、cookie、登录状态、两步验证都在，不用再登录一次。 不抢屏幕：任务在后台窗口里跑，页面会被告知“有焦点”，你在别的软件里打字也不受影响。 有围栏：扩展只碰你在扩展设置页里允许的网站，并且只接受带本地密钥的任务；白名单只能在扩展自己的设置页改，Agent 改不了。 很小：只用 Python 标准库，没有 npm，不用构建，核心约 1100 行。 是命令行，不是 MCP 服务，任何能跑 shell 命令的 Agent（包括 Claude Code）都能用。 和 Playwright / Puppeteer 比：做测试、跑在服务器上请用它们；Tabrelay 取舍的是“在你已经在用的浏览器里干活”，所以没有自动等待定位器，只支持 Chrome/Chromium，页面也能检测到调试器已连接。 sh tabrelay ping TAB=$(tabrelay open ) tabrelay eval "$TAB" 'document.title' tabrelay shot "$TAB" /tmp/example.png 项目才一周，欢迎试用、提意见。开发中大量使用了 AI 编程助手（Claude Code）。
